## Step 3 — On serial entry (blur), fetch history and write into the lane row

You already have `fetch_repaired_pcb_for_serial(frm, row, serial)`.

Upgrade it so it also sets these 4 new lane fields.

In client script, update that function like this:

```js
function fetch_repaired_pcb_for_serial(frm, row, serial) {
  if (!serial || !row?.name || frm.is_new()) return;

  frappe.call({
    method: "pts1_api",
    args: { api_cmd: "get_lane_result_by_serial", serial: serial },
    freeze: false,
    callback(r) {
      const m = r?.message;
      if (!m?.ok) return;

      const cdt = row.doctype || (frm.fields_dict.lanes?.grid?.df?.options);
      const cdn = row.name;
      const lane_no = row.lane_no || 0;

      // ----- Update lane UI fields (local) -----
      if (cdt && cdn) {
        if (m.repaired_pcb) frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "repaired_pcb", 1);

        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "last_dump_status", (m.dump_status || ""));
        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "last_dump_at", (m.dump_last_at || ""));
        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "last_flash_status", (m.flash_status || ""));
        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "last_flash_at", (m.flash_last_at || ""));
      }

      frm.refresh_field("lanes");
      if (frm.fields_dict.lane_dashboard) render_lane_dashboard(frm);

      // ----- Persist to DB so it survives reload -----
      if (lane_no && frm.doc.name) {
        frappe.call({
          method: "pts1_api",
          args: {
            api_cmd: "update_lane_fields",
            docname: frm.doc.name,
            lane_no: lane_no,
            fields: {
              repaired_pcb: m.repaired_pcb ? 1 : 0,
              last_dump_status: (m.dump_status || ""),
              last_dump_at: (m.dump_last_at || ""),
              last_flash_status: (m.flash_status || ""),
              last_flash_at: (m.flash_last_at || "")
            }
          },
          freeze: false
        });
      }
    }
  });
```
```js
}
```

### Current behavior (with the code we have now)

- **If you CLEAR the serial (make it blank) in a lane row**:
  - That row is **fully reset**:
    - `pcb_serial_no` becomes empty
    - `com_port` becomes empty
    - `mac_id`, `lane_status`, `lane_action(_status/message)`, `lane_progress`, `lane_step`, `error_message`, `lane_log`, `lane_result_json`, `fw_file` are all cleared / reset.
  - Visually: only `Lane No` (and the row index) remain; all other columns go blank/default.

- **If you CHANGE the serial from one non‑empty value to another non‑empty value**:
  - The row is **logically reset for a new PCB**, but **COM port is kept**:
    - New `pcb_serial_no` is set.
    - `lane_status`, `lane_action(_status/message)`, `lane_progress`, `lane_step`, `error_message`, `lane_log`, `mac_id`, `lane_result_json`, `fw_file` are cleared / reset.
    - `com_port` is preserved so you don’t have to re‑scan COMs.
  - Then when you press Dump/Flash for that lane, **all new info for that PCB** (log, MAC, status, etc.) will be filled for that same row.

So:

- **“Resetting lane = row becomes empty”** is true when you clear the serial (blank).  
- When you enter a **new serial**, the row is reset except for COM (by design); all new test info will belong to that serial once you run Dump/Flash.

If you instead want the row to truly be empty (including COM) every time the serial changes (even non‑blank), I can switch it so COM is also cleared on any serial change.

## ✅ 1) BIG BUG in `append_lane_log`: your run_id check is wrong

You wrote:

```python
cur_run_id = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id") or "").strip()
if not cur_run_id and incoming_run_id:
    out = {"ok": False, "reason": "run_id_mismatch"}
elif incoming_run_id and cur_run_id and cur_run_id != incoming_run_id:
    out = {"ok": False, ...}
else:
   append...
```

This **rejects log append** when:

* DB run_id is blank (can happen if field wasn’t saved / custom field missing / claim didn’t set it because it already existed as blank / migration bug)
* connector sends run_id (always)

So logs will **never reach ERP** even though connector is running.

### ✅ Correct logic

* If DB has run_id, incoming must match.
* If DB has no run_id, and incoming has run_id, **set DB run_id to incoming and accept** (this is safe because lane is already Running/Requested on this lane row).
* If incoming run_id missing, reject (because your update_lane_fields now requires run_id for active lanes).

#### Replace your whole `append_lane_log` guard with this:

```python
cur_run_id = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id") or "").strip()

# If DB has run_id, incoming must match
if cur_run_id and incoming_run_id and cur_run_id != incoming_run_id:
    out = {"ok": False, "api_cmd": api_cmd, "reason": "run_id_mismatch"}
# If DB has NO run_id but incoming has one, adopt it
elif (not cur_run_id) and incoming_run_id:
    try:
        frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id", incoming_run_id, update_modified=False)
        cur_run_id = incoming_run_id
    except Exception:
        pass
    # proceed to append
    # (no out here)
# If lane is active but incoming has no run_id, reject
elif not incoming_run_id:
    out = {"ok": False, "api_cmd": api_cmd, "reason": "missing_run_id"}
else:
    # proceed
    pass
```

Then the append logic continues.

Fetch run_id first from row you already have (`row.get("run_id")`) and pass it:

```py
rid = safe_str(row.get("run_id"))
fields = {"com_port": newv}
if rid:
    fields["run_id"] = rid
lane_update(docname, lane_no, fields)
```

## ✅ 3) Connector: you added heartbeat retry + reassert Running ✅ (good)

Your new heartbeat block is solid. One improvement:

### ✅ Make heartbeat use `lane_update_verified` instead of raw API

Reason: raw call only checks `ok`; but if server returns `field_write_failed` or `run_id_mismatch`, you should log it clearly.

Minimal change: keep as is, but print server reason when hb_ok is false:

```py
msg = msg or {}
if not hb_ok:
    print("[HEARTBEAT NACK]", docname, lane_no, msg)
```

---

## ✅ 4) Small server improvement: `claim_lane` should always return DB run_id

You already return:

```python
effective_run_id = (db run_id) or run_id
out = {"run_id": effective_run_id}
```

Good.

But you currently only set run_id if `not cur_run_id and run_id`.

If cur_run_id exists but is wrong/stale from an older run, you will keep it. That can cause run_id mismatch later.

### ✅ Fix (recommended)

When claiming, always set run_id to the incoming one **because claim is the atomic moment of a run**.

Replace:

```python
if not cur_run_id and run_id:
    set run_id
effective_run_id = db run_id or run_id
```

With:

```python
if run_id:
    try:
        frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id", run_id, update_modified=False)
    except Exception:
        pass
effective_run_id = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id") or "").strip() or run_id
```

This makes claim authoritative.

## Fixes applied

### Fix A: Auto-refresh skips reload when form is dirty

### Fix B: Dump/Flash – commit and patch before request
1. **`commit_active_grid_cell()`** – Blurs the active input so the grid commits the current cell into the model.
2. **`lane_patch_to_db(frm, lane_no)`** – Sends `pcb_serial_no`, `com_port`, and `repaired_pcb` to the server via `update_lane_fields`.
3. **`request_action()`** – Updated to:
   - Call `commit_active_grid_cell()` first.
   - Validate serial and COM from the model.
   - Call `lane_patch_to_db()` before `request_lane_action`.
   - Then call `request_lane_action`.

Result: Lane values are written to the DB before the server validates them, so the 417 “PCB Serial No and COM Port are required” error should be resolved.

### Fix C: No reload in `save_lane_via_api`
- Already in place; `save_lane_via_api` does not call `reload_doc()`.

Now you have a solid, no‑manual solution.

### What changed for **Stop / Reset**

- **Server `abort_lane` (PTS1 API script)**:
  - When you press **Reset** on a **busy** lane, the client calls `api_cmd = "abort_lane"`.
  - I changed `abort_lane` to behave as a **force stop + reset** on ERP:
    - Sets `lane_action_message = "Aborted by user"`.
    - Sets `lane_action_status = ""`.
    - Sets `lane_status = "Pending"`.
    - Sets `lane_progress = 0`, `lane_step = ""`.
    - Clears `run_id`, `connector_name`, `last_heartbeat_at`.
  - So after the call, the lane is **clean and idle**, ready for a fresh Dump/Flash, even if the connector process is dead.

- **Client `reset_lane` (PTS1 client script)**:
  - In the **busy** path it still calls `abort_lane`, but after success it now:
    - Calls `frm.reload_doc()`.
    - Shows toast: “Lane X stopped and reset”.
  - Net effect: one click on **Reset** while Running/Requested will always leave that lane **Pending** in UI and DB.

### What you do now

- If a lane misbehaves or gets stuck:
  - Just press **Reset** on that lane.
  - It will **stop + reset** the lane state; you can immediately re‑run Dump/Flash and later Upload.
- You should no longer see a lane stuck in `AbortRequested` blocking uploads; reset will clear it automatically.

### Short answer

Those two structural issues are already fixed in the version you just pasted. You’re now in the “production‑stable” shape you described.

### How your current code matches the rules

- **No server writes on blur anymore**
  - `save_lane_via_api` and `debounced_autosave` are gone from `setup_auto_reset_on_serial_change`.
  - Blur handler only:
    - Reads `new_serial` (captured / DOM / model).
    - Updates the model.
    - Clears lane fields **locally**.
    - Does a small delayed `refresh_field("lanes")`.

- **Serial change: set serial first, then clear (without touching serial)**
  - On serial cleared:
    - `frappe.model.set_value(..., "pcb_serial_no", "")`
    - `clear_lane_row(..., KEEP_COM_ON_CLEAR)` (this is OK because we explicitly set serial to empty).
  - On serial changed:
    - `frappe.model.set_value(..., "pcb_serial_no", new_serial);`
    - `clear_lane_row_keep_serial(..., KEEP_COM_ON_NEW_SERIAL);`  
      `clear_lane_row_keep_serial` deletes `pcb_serial_no` from the cleared fields, so serial is never wiped.

- **No competing save paths**
  - Blur handler is **UI-only**.
  - The only place that pushes lane to DB is:
    - `request_action` → `commit_active_grid_cell()` → `lane_patch_to_db()` → `request_lane_action`.
  - Find COM / Reset / Upload still go through `pts1_api` as expected.

- **Dirty-safe reloads**
  - `start_auto_refresh_if_needed` and the Find COM poll both skip `frm.reload_doc()` when `frm.is_dirty()` is true.

So the two concerns in your note (aggressive auto-reset + double save paths) are already resolved in this code. It’s safe to test now: lanes 2–4 should keep their serials, and Dump/Flash should not hit the “required” 417 error due to stale DB values.

### Why **Lane Flash Log** stayed empty

1. **`setattr(res, "lane_flash_log", …)` in a Server Script** often **does not reliably save**. Frappe’s scripted API is safer with **`frappe.db.set_value`** after the document is saved.
2. The old helper ran **before** `insert()` / `save()`, which is fragile for new docs and for how Server Scripts treat the in-memory `Document`.
3. **`meta.has_field(...)`** can fail or block in some setups even when the field exists, so the code could **exit early** and do nothing.

So **`lane_result_json` updated** (normal `res.save()` path) but the mirror to **Lane Flash Log** never made it to the DB.

### What we changed

In **`pts api server script 02-03-2026 - Copy.py`**:

- Replaced the old helper with **`mirror_lane_run_into_pts1_lane_result_archive(...)`**, which runs **after** `res.insert()` / `res.save()` and writes with **`frappe.db.set_value("PTS1 Lane Result", res.name, fld, ...)`**.
- Each flash/dump run now prepends (newest first):
  - the **same compact line** as in `lane_result_json` (`ts=…|op=flash|…`), and  
  - the **full `lane_log`** from the **PTS1 Test** lane row (same idea as the grid “Lane 2 Log”), with the same **`--- FLASH | … ---`** style header as on the child table.
- API response now includes **`lane_result_archive_saved`**: `true` if the DB write succeeded, `false` if it failed (e.g. wrong field name / column missing).

### What you should do on ERPNext

1. **Paste/replace** the updated Server Script in **Server Script** `pts1_api` (or whatever runs `record_lane_run`).

Yes — **this is good enough to run** and it should **fix your Lane 2/3/4 “Serial+COM required” error**.

But there are **3 specific places** where your current server script can still create random issues (lane overwrite / wrong doctype / race). Fix these 3 and it becomes **stable**.

---

# ✅ 1) `reset_lane` block has WRONG child doctype

You wrote:

```py
child_dt = getattr(row, "doctype", None) or "PTS1 Lane"
```

This is risky because:

* Your actual child table doctype may NOT be `"PTS1 Lane"`.
* If it’s wrong, reset will silently fail or update wrong table.

### ✅ Replace ONLY this line in `reset_lane`:

```py
child_dt = getattr(row, "doctype", None) or "PTS1 Lane"
```

### With this:

```py
child_dt = frappe.get_meta("PTS1 Test").get_field("lanes").options
```

That’s it.

---

# ✅ 2) `update_find_com_result` still uses `doc.save()` (can overwrite other lanes)

Your `update_find_com_result` does:

* doc = get_doc
* row.com_port set in memory
* `doc.save()`

If connector is updating lane1 log/progress at the same time, this `doc.save()` can **write back an older snapshot** and wipe a lane log/progress.

### ✅ Fix (simple + safe)

Inside `update_find_com_result`, change only the “assign ports” part to DB atomic writes.

#### Find this part:

```py
if status == "Done" and ports:
    ports_list = to_list(ports)
    lanes = sorted((doc.lanes or []), key=lambda r: int(r.lane_no or 0))
    i = 0
    for row in lanes:
        if i < len(ports_list):
            row.com_port = str(ports_list[i])
        i += 1

doc.save(ignore_permissions=True)
```

#### Replace ONLY that with:

```py
if status == "Done" and ports:
    ports_list = to_list(ports)
    child_dt = frappe.get_meta("PTS1 Test").get_field("lanes").options
    lanes = sorted((doc.lanes or []), key=lambda r: int(r.lane_no or 0))
    i = 0
    for row in lanes:
        if i < len(ports_list):
            try:
                frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "com_port", str(ports_list[i]), update_modified=False)
            except Exception:
                pass
        i += 1

# keep parent fields update (either doc.save OR better: db.set_value)
doc.save(ignore_permissions=True)
```

**Minimum change**: atomic child updates.
(Parent save is ok here because it only changes parent fields; if you want 100% atomic, tell me and I’ll give the parent-only db.set_value version too.)

---

# ✅ 3) `request_find_com` uses `doc.save()` (not a big issue, but make it atomic)

Not mandatory, but best:

Replace:

```py
doc = get_pts_doc(docname)
doc.find_com_status = "Requested"
doc.find_com_message = ""
doc.save(ignore_permissions=True)
frappe.db.commit()
```

With:

```py
frappe.db.set_value("PTS1 Test", docname, "find_com_status", "Requested", update_modified=False)
frappe.db.set_value("PTS1 Test", docname, "find_com_message", "", update_modified=False)
frappe.db.commit()
```

### What this means for you in practice

- **If a lane shows “AbortRequested” and you click Upload:**
  - Now ERP will **not** try to upload.
  - You’ll get a clear message like:  
    “Upload is not allowed while Abort is requested. Wait for the lane to finish Aborting, then re-run Flash if needed.”

### What you should do step‑by‑step

1. **See lane status = AbortRequested / Aborting / Aborted**
   - Do **not** press Upload.

2. **Wait for the connector to finish aborting**
   - Lane should move to a stable state (usually not `Done`), or you can `Reset` that lane.

3. **Then decide:**
   - If you still want a result for this PCB:
     - Press **Flash** again (fresh run, should go to `Done` when successful).
     - When it is `Done` (and status looks correct), press **Upload**.
   - If that PCB is truly scrapped:
     - You can leave it un-uploaded (or handle it in your process), but **don’t upload from an aborted run**.

So you don’t need to “fix” anything here—this guard is just **protecting** you from uploading from a half‑aborted run. Your action: **only upload after a clean `Done` state; if abort happens, redo Flash before uploading.**

- The real reason is **in the worker’s own printed output right before it exits** (it typically prints which step failed: ISP cache, device not detected, flash/dump failed, file not found, COM not accessible, etc.).

### Immediate quick checks (most common causes)
- **Wrong COM / device missing**: if COM was blank or changed, you’ll see “device not found” / “not in ISP device cache”.
- **XUV/HTF path missing**: worker prints file path errors.
- **Tool executable missing**: `NvsCmd.exe` / `ConfigCmd.exe` not found.
- **USB relay/modbus error**: you’ll see connect errors (sometimes non-fatal, sometimes fatal depending on your code).

function clear_lane_row_keep_serial(cdt, cdn, keep_com) {
  const fields = get_cleared_lane_fields(keep_com);
  Object.keys(fields).forEach((k) => {
    if (k === "pcb_serial_no") return; // hard guard

  });

If someone later adds pcb_serial_no into cleared fields, this prevents disaster.

if (typeof frm.is_dirty === "function" && frm.is_dirty()) return;

const ae = document.activeElement;
const typingNow = ae && (ae.tagName === "INPUT" || ae.tagName === "TEXTAREA") && $(ae).closest(".grid-row, .frappe-control").length;
if (typingNow) return;

if (typeof frm.is_dirty === "function" && frm.is_dirty()) return;

Here is what was going wrong and what we changed.

## Why flash “passed” but post-flash MAC failed

1. **`ConfigCmd ... MERGE` returning `Success` is not enough**  
   Your log shows `WARNING: No configuration data found` during merge. The tool can still exit successfully while the **on-disk HTF** does not get a clean, parseable Bluetooth block (LAP/UAP/NAP or BD_ADDR) in the layout `read_mac_from_htf_file()` expects.

2. **Dump vs flash were asymmetric**  
   After a **dump**, you run **`dev2txt`** and pull the device config into the HTF, so MAC parsing usually works. After **flash**, you only ran **`txt2dev ... MERGE`** and then tried to parse the **same file** without re-reading from the chip. So the hardware steps could all pass while the **file** still had nothing the parser could read.

3. **`'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write_coil'`**  
   Log says **`Modbus Relays in Signal Tray status: NOT CONNECTED`**, but the code still called `relay_obj.setState_ON_OFF(...)` whenever `relay_obj` was not `None`. Some stacks return a **non-`None` wrapper** with a **`None` Modbus client**, which triggers exactly that error on `write_coil`.

---

## What we changed in `ERP_PTS-1.py` (in your repo copy)

1. **After a successful MERGE**, run the same **`ConfigCmd.exe dev2txt ...`** step you use on dump, then parse MAC / update the sheet. That refreshes the HTF from the device so LAP/UAP/NAP (or equivalent) can appear in the file.

2. **Stronger HTF parsing** (already in your file):  
   - `_mac_from_scattered_lap_uap_nap` — LAP/UAP/NAP on **non-adjacent** lines  
   - Extra patterns for **12-hex** BD-style addresses  

3. **`_relay_status_connected()`** — only turn the USB relay **OFF** when the status string clearly indicates **connected**, and **never** when it looks like **NOT CONNECTED** / disconnected / offline. That avoids `write_coil` on a dead client.

4. **`rl_status`** is initialized and set from `relay()` so the `finally` block can use it safely.

---

## What you should do on the bench PC

- Deploy the updated **`ERP_PTS-1.py`** to the path the **PTS1 Station Connector** actually runs (often under `D:\PTS_1\...` or similar — not only the Desktop copy).

If **`dev2txt` fails** after MERGE, you’ll get a **warning** and we still try parsing the old file; in that case fix COM/tooling for `dev2txt`, or open the HTF and confirm whether LAP/UAP/NAP (or BD_ADDR) lines exist.

## Fix: Serial cleared in lanes 2, 3, 4 after Enter

### Root cause

1. **Value lost before blur** – On Enter, the grid can clear or reset the cell before the blur handler runs.
2. **Order of updates** – Clearing the lane before setting the serial could overwrite the value.
3. **Refresh timing** – Refreshing the grid too early could read stale data.

### Changes made

1. **Capture value on Enter before blur**
   - On Enter, read the value from the input and store it in `frm.__pts1_enter_captured`.
   - Blur handler uses this stored value first, then DOM, then model.

2. **Update order**
   - Set `pcb_serial_no` first.
   - Then clear other lane fields.
   - Ensures the serial is in the model before any refresh.

3. **Deferred refresh**
   - Call `refresh_field("lanes")` inside `setTimeout(0)` so the model is updated before the grid re-renders.

4. **Error handling**
   - If the API call fails, show a message and do not reload.

5. **Captured value cleanup**
   - Clear the captured value only when it is used for the matching row.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
`com_scan_headless.py` only looked at **USB PnP** devices whose **friendly name ended with** something like `- 112`. On many Win10/11 setups the name looks like **`USB Serial Port (COM107)`**, so **no rows** were returned, grouping stayed empty, and you always got `ports = []`.

### Fixes (in your project copy)

1. **`com_scan_headless.py`**
   - **Tier 0:** If **pyserial** is installed, use `serial.tools.list_ports` first (fast and reliable).
   - **Tier 1:** Same USB PnP scan as before.
   - **Tier 2:** If that returns no rows, run **`Get-CimInstance Win32_SerialPort`** so normal COM devices still show up.
   - **`com_from_best_device_name`** now understands **`(COM123)`** and trailing **`COM123`**, not only `- 112`.

2. **`PTS1 Station Connector.py` — `run_com_scan()`**
   - Logs **stderr**, **empty stdout**, **bad JSON**, and **`ok: false`** with the error so the next failure is obvious in the console.

### What you should do on the Lenono PC
Copy the updated  
`com_scan_headless.py`  
to the path the connector actually uses (**`D:\PTS_1\PTS_1\com_scan_headless.py`** per your log).

### How your current code matches the rules

### AI  ``

Here’s how it behaves with the code you have now.

### `COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "right"` (current default)

The scan only gives a **flat list** of COM numbers (e.g. `['106','114','107']`). There is **no** notion of “which physical lane is empty” inside that list.

With **3** numbers and **right** alignment we do:

| Lane | COM   |
|------|--------|
| 1    | empty  |
| 2    | 106    |
| 3    | 114    |
| 4    | 107    |

So you get **`nil, 106, 114, 107`**-style behavior: **leading** lanes stay empty, values are packed **toward lane 4**.

### Why not `112, nil, 114, 107`?

That pattern means “something in slot 2 is missing but slot 1 still has 112.” The scanner would have to return **four slots** (with an explicit empty in the middle). Today **`com_scan_headless`** only returns **connected** COMs, so a list like `['112','114','107']` is **three** devices — with **right** mode that becomes **`nil, 112, 114, 107`**, not `112, nil, 114, 107`.

So:

- **Yes**: missing COMs show as **empty** on the ERP lane.
- **Leading** empties when there are fewer than 4 ports → use **`right`** (what you want for “port 1 empty”).
- **A hole in the middle** (`112, nil, 114, 107`) would need the scan (or another mapping) to output **placeholders per fixed slot**; the connector alone cannot infer that from `['112','114','107']`.

### `COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "left"`

With the same three ports you get **`106, 114, 107, nil`** (fill from lane 1, **clear** any extra lane at the end). Still no automatic middle `nil`.

### 2. **Lane 1–4 ↔ USB slots (no left/right packing for USB scan)**
**`com_scan_headless.py`**
- Builds **`slots`**: a list of **4** strings — COM for that USB “slot”, or `""` if nothing there.

- Example: only physical **port 2** → often `["", "106", "", ""]` → **only lane 2** gets `106`.

- **`COM_PORT_FALLBACK_MODE = "left"`**: if there is **no** `slots` (pyserial/CIM-only), COMs are filled with **left** packing (change to `"right"` if you prefer).
- **`run_com_scan()`** returns **`(ports, slots)`**; background scan compares a signature that includes `slots`.

**Server script `update_find_com_result`**

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
`com_scan_headless.py` only looked at **USB PnP** devices whose **friendly name ended with** something like `- 112`. On many Win10/11 setups the name looks like **`USB Serial Port (COM107)`**, so **no rows** were returned, grouping stayed empty, and you always got `ports = []`.

### Fixes (in your project copy)

1. **`com_scan_headless.py`**
   - **Tier 0:** If **pyserial** is installed, use `serial.tools.list_ports` first (fast and reliable).
   - **Tier 1:** Same USB PnP scan as before.
   - **Tier 2:** If that returns no rows, run **`Get-CimInstance Win32_SerialPort`** so normal COM devices still show up.
   - **`com_from_best_device_name`** now understands **`(COM123)`** and trailing **`COM123`**, not only `- 112`.

2. **`PTS1 Station Connector.py` — `run_com_scan()`**
   - Logs **stderr**, **empty stdout**, **bad JSON**, and **`ok: false`** with the error so the next failure is obvious in the console.

### AI  ``

## Field type: use Check, not Data

The **Repaired PCB** field should store **Yes/No** (repaired or not), not the PCB serial.

- **PCB serial** is already in `pcb_serial_no`.
- **Repaired PCB** should indicate whether the BT module was replaced (Yes/No).

So:

- Use **Check** (checkbox) for `repaired_pcb`.
- Do **not** use **Data** for this field.

If you keep it as Data, you’d have to handle values like "Yes"/"No"/"1"/"0" manually and the UI would be unclear.

---

## Flow 1: Normal PCB (not repaired)

**Condition:** `repaired_pcb` = No (unchecked)

**Config file:** `{base_serial}_config.htf`  
Example: `111_config.htf`

**Dump:**
- Uses base serial (e.g. `111`).
- Writes to `111_config.htf` (creates or overwrites).
- Adds `111` to sheet only if not already there.
- MAC comes from this original file.

**Flash:**
- Uses base serial `111`.
- Reads `111_config.htf`.
- Burns firmware and writes MAC from this file.

**Logic:** One MAC per PCB, one config file per serial.

---

## Flow 2: Repaired PCB (BT module replaced)

**Condition:** `repaired_pcb` = Yes (checked)

**Config file:** `{base_serial}_N_config.htf` (versioned)  
Example: `111_1_config.htf`, `111_2_config.htf`, etc.

**Dump:**
- Uses next version (e.g. `111_2`).
- Writes to `111_2_config.htf`.
- Adds `111_2` to sheet.
- MAC comes from the new BT module.

**Flash:**
- Uses latest version for that base serial (e.g. `111_2`).
- Reads `111_2_config.htf`.
- Burns firmware and writes MAC from this file.

**Logic:** New BT module → new MAC → new config file; versioning keeps history.

---

## Summary

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `pcb_serial_no` | PCB serial (e.g. `111`) |
| `repaired_pcb` | Yes/No: was BT module replaced? |

Change `repaired_pcb` to **Check** in PTS1 Lane Result (and PTS1 Lane if needed) so it stores a boolean, not the serial.

### AI  ``

Here’s when that empty lane gets a COM again.

### Automatic (station connector running)

1. **How often it scans**  
   About every **`COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC`** seconds (default **2.0**), the connector runs `com_scan_headless.py`.

2. **When ERP lanes are updated**  
   It only calls `auto_update_com_ports_for_doc` when the **new port list is different** from the last one (`ports != last_ports`). So when you plug a board into a lane that was empty, as soon as Windows shows an extra COM and the scan returns a **changed** list (e.g. 3 → 4 ports, or different numbers), the next successful scan after that will push updates.

3. **Typical delay**  
   Roughly **2–4 seconds** after the device is enumerated (one interval + scan time), **if** the connector is running and the doc is in **`list_jobs_for_pc`** for that PC.

4. **When a lane is skipped**  
   If **`COM_UPDATE_ONLY_WHEN_IDLE = True`**, COM is only written for lanes whose **`lane_action_status`** is **empty** or **`Done`**. A lane that is **Requested / Running / …** won’t get its COM auto-changed until it’s idle again.

### Manual

Use **Find COM Ports** on the PTS1 form when you want an immediate scan without waiting for the background interval (that path uses the server/API flow you already have).

### If it seems slow

- Lower **`COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC`** (e.g. `1.0`) for quicker retries.  
- Ensure the connector process stays running on that PC.

Those two structural issues are already fixed in the version you just pasted. You’re now in the “production‑stable” shape you described.

### How your current code matches the rules

- **No server writes on blur anymore**
  - `save_lane_via_api` and `debounced_autosave` are gone from `setup_auto_reset_on_serial_change`.

  - `start_auto_refresh_if_needed` and the Find COM poll both skip `frm.reload_doc()` when `frm.is_dirty()` is true.

But to make it **fully reliable** (no “stuck in Requested” feeling + no manual refresh dependency), you still need **3 small additions** around it.

Right now your code updates the grid only **when `poll_status_snapshot()` is actually running**. So the real question is: *“Is polling guaranteed to start and keep running at the right time?”*
If polling doesn’t start immediately after queue, or if it stops early, you will again feel manual refresh.

# ✅ 1) Your block is correct (keep it)

Your `apply_snapshot_to_grid()` + `poll_status_snapshot()` are fine.

Only one improvement inside `apply_snapshot_to_grid()`:

### Add “do not refresh if operator is typing inside grid”

Otherwise, when you type serial in lane2 while lane1 running, it can still annoy.

Add this guard at the top:

```js
const ae = document.activeElement;
const typingNow =
  ae &&
  (ae.tagName === "INPUT" || ae.tagName === "TEXTAREA") &&
  $(ae).closest(".grid-row").length;

if (typingNow) return;
```

So final:

```js
function apply_snapshot_to_grid(frm, snapshot) {
  if (!snapshot || !snapshot.lanes || !frm.doc.lanes) return;

  const ae = document.activeElement;
  const typingNow =
    ae &&
    (ae.tagName === "INPUT" || ae.tagName === "TEXTAREA") &&
    $(ae).closest(".grid-row").length;

  if (typingNow) return;

  const runtimeKeys = [
    "lane_status",
    "lane_action",
    "lane_action_status",
    "lane_progress",
    "lane_action_message",
    "error_message",
    "mac_id",
    "lane_log"
  ];

  snapshot.lanes.forEach((live) => {
    const local = (frm.doc.lanes || []).find((r) => Number(r.lane_no) === Number(live.lane_no));
    if (!local) return;

    runtimeKeys.forEach((k) => {
      if (live[k] !== undefined) local[k] = live[k];
    });
  });

  frm.refresh_field("lanes");
}
```

---

# ✅ 2) Make polling start immediately after Queue (VERY IMPORTANT)

If you don’t do this, you will see:
Queued/Requested stays for some time until timer starts → feels stuck → you refresh manually.

### Where to add:

Inside your `request_action(...).then(() => { ... })` success block.

Add this line at the end:

```js
poll_status_snapshot(frm);
```

Example:

```js
.then(() => {
  const r = lane_row(frm, lane_no);
  if (r) {
    r.lane_action = action;
    r.lane_action_status = "Requested";
    r.lane_status = "Queued";
    r.lane_progress = 0;
    r.lane_action_message = "";
    r.error_message = "";
  }

  frm.refresh_field("lanes");
  render_lane_dashboard(frm);
  start_auto_refresh_if_needed(frm);

  poll_status_snapshot(frm); // ✅ start immediately
  frappe.show_alert({ message: `Lane ${lane_no} queued for ${action}`, indicator: "blue" });
})
```

---

# ✅ 3) Fix your `start_auto_refresh_if_needed()` so it ALWAYS polls (not reload)

You already changed it mostly, but confirm this exact behavior:

### What it must do:

* if any lane is Requested/Running (from snapshot OR frm.doc) → start a timer
* timer should call `poll_status_snapshot(frm)` every 1–2 sec
* should NOT require `reload_doc()` at all

So inside the timer: **only call poll_status_snapshot**.

Example pattern:

```js
function start_auto_refresh_if_needed(frm) {
  const shouldRun = anyLaneActive(frm) || anyLaneActiveFromSnapshot(frm.__pts1_live);

  if (shouldRun && !frm.__lane_timer) {
    frm.__lane_timer = setInterval(() => {
      const ae = document.activeElement;
      const typingNow =
        ae &&
        (ae.tagName === "INPUT" || ae.tagName === "TEXTAREA") &&
        $(ae).closest(".grid-row, .frappe-control").length;
      if (typingNow) return;

      poll_status_snapshot(frm);
    }, 1500);

    poll_status_snapshot(frm); // ✅ first shot immediately
  }

  if (!shouldRun && frm.__lane_timer) {
    clearInterval(frm.__lane_timer);
    frm.__lane_timer = null;
  }
}
```

---

# ✅ 4) One more thing you MUST understand (important expectation)

Even after this, the blue banner:

> “This form has been modified after you have loaded it”

may still appear sometimes, because connector is changing DB in background.

But your UI will still show correct live status, so the operator doesn’t need to click Refresh.

If you want to reduce that banner frequency:
You must avoid `frm.reload_doc()` entirely during runs (you are already doing that now).

---

# Bottom line

✅ Your block is **correct**, but **not sufficient alone** unless you also:

1. trigger first poll right after queue
2. ensure timer keeps polling
3. avoid updating grid while typing

Do these 3 and you will get:

* live Running/Completed without reload
* operator can keep typing serials in other lanes

### AI  ``

Here’s what was going wrong and what to do.

### 1. `Unknown column 'find_com_status'` (COM Ports OK button)

The **Server Script** is fine; the **database** has no columns for those fields. The script was doing `SET find_com_status = ...` on **`tabPTS1 Test`**, and MySQL returned **1054** because those columns don’t exist.

**Fix on ERPNext**

1. **Customize Form** → DocType **PTS1 Test**.
2. Add:
   - **`find_com_status`** — type **Data** (e.g. length 50).
   - **`find_com_message`** — type **Small Text** or **Text**.
3. **Save**.
4. On the server shell (same env as the site):

   `bench migrate`

After migrate, the COM Ports OK / Find COM flow can write those fields.

In your repo copy of the server script, a small helper **`db_set_find_com_parent`** is used for those writes. If the column error still happens, you’ll get a **clear Frappe message** telling you to add those fields and run **`bench migrate`**, instead of a raw PyMySQL traceback.

Paste the updated script into **Server Script** `pts1_api` after you pull the file from the project.

---

### 2. Lane 1 has a PCB but COM looks empty

With **`COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "right"`** and only **three** COM numbers from the scan (`['106','114','107']`), the mapping is **by design**:

| Lane | COM   |
|------|--------|
| 1    | *(empty)* |
| 2    | 106   |
| 3    | 114   |
| 4    | 107   |

So **lane 1 stays empty** until the scan returns **four** ports (or you switch mode).

Your log also shows the list changing (`['106','107']` → `['106','114','107']`), which usually means **Windows is sometimes not showing one device** (cable, hub, driver). If the board on lane 1 doesn’t always appear as a fourth COM, lane 1 will stay blank in **right** mode.

**If scan order is always lane 1 → lane 4** when all four are present, use:

`COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "left"`

Then with three ports you get **106, 114, 107** on lanes **1–3** and lane **4** cleared—not “empty lane 1”.

**Summary**

- **Right**: use when the **first** physical slot is often empty and you want COMs **packed toward lane 4**.
- **Left**: use when **missing** devices are at the **end** (or scan order matches 1→4 from the top).

---

### 3. After you add `find_com_*` fields

The connector’s **Find COM** polling uses **`find_com_status == Requested`**. Once the columns exist and you click COM Ports OK, status can move to **Requested → Running → Done** and the connector can run the scan and push COMs as before.

## 1) 🚨 BUG: `append_lane_log` does `chunk = ... .strip()` (still bad)

You removed `.strip()` on merged ✅, but you still do:

```python
chunk = (payload.get("chunk") or "").strip()
```

That will delete trailing `\n` and can merge lines badly (and also lose beginning spaces/log formatting).

### ✅ Fix

Change to:

```python
chunk = (payload.get("chunk") or "")
```

No strip.

---

## 2) 🚨 BUG: Heartbeat is NOT updating if `update_lane_fields` is blocked / fails

In connector you send:

```py
hb_fields["last_heartbeat_at"] = 1
lane_update(...)
```

Server converts any `last_heartbeat_at` write into `frappe.utils.now()` ✅

But: if your lane_update gets **field_write_failed**, you only print heartbeat fail; you do **not** retry heartbeat. If heartbeat stops for >120s, your server will mark stale even though connector is alive but had transient write failures.

### ✅ Fix (connector)

On heartbeat failure, do **one retry** quickly:

```python
try:
    lane_update(docname, lane_no, hb_fields)
except Exception:
    try:
        time.sleep(0.2)
        lane_update(docname, lane_no, hb_fields)
    except Exception as e2:
        print("[HEARTBEAT FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e2))
```

Also: include **lane_action_status="Running"** in heartbeat fields (optional but helps recover from accidental UI overwrites):

```python
hb_fields["lane_action_status"] = "Running"
hb_fields["lane_status"] = "Running"
```

Server allows these fields; run_id guard protects it.

---

## 3) ⚠️ DATA RACE: `reset_lane` can be called while connector still appending logs

Scenario:

* lane becomes Stale
* user clicks Reset (server clears lane_log, statuses, run_id stays? you clear statuses but you do **not** clear run_id)
* connector is still alive and still has log_cache and still calls append_lane_log with old run_id
* server will accept append because run_id still matches (or cur_run_id empty) → lane log repopulates after reset.

### ✅ Fix (server reset_lane)

When resetting, **also clear run_id** so old connector updates get rejected:

Add:

```python
try:
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id", "", update_modified=False)
except Exception:
    pass
```

And also clear:

```python
try:
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "connector_name", "", update_modified=False)
except Exception:
    pass
try:
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "last_heartbeat_at", None, update_modified=False)
except Exception:
    pass
```

Now old append_lane_log with old run_id will be rejected (run_id_mismatch).

---

## 4) ⚠️ `claim_lane` still allows “running without run_id” if UI didn’t set it

Edge-case: UI didn’t save run_id field (field missing / custom field not added / permission), but connector passes fallback doc|lane. claim_lane will set run_id, ok.

But: your `update_lane_fields` guard only blocks when both incoming_run_id and cur_run_id exist. If cur_run_id is empty and connector forgets to send run_id once, it will update without guard.

### ✅ Fix (server update_lane_fields)

Make run_id **mandatory for all connector updates after claim** by enforcing:

* if lane_action_status is Running/Done/Stale/AbortRequested, require incoming_run_id.

Add this before allowed writes:

```python
cur_status = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, row.name, "lane_action_status") or "").strip().lower()

if cur_status in ("running", "done", "stale", "abortrequested"):
    if not incoming_run_id:
        out = {"ok": False, "api_cmd": api_cmd, "reason": "missing_run_id"}
        frappe.response["message"] = out
        return
```

This forces connector to always send run_id (which you already do via fields_base).

# Quick sanity check on your overall architecture

✅ You’ve now implemented the “correct pattern”:

* **Queue**: request_lane_action writes run_id + Requested
* **Claim**: claim_lane flips to Running and returns authoritative run_id
* **Updates**: all updates carry run_id guard
* **Logs**: append-only server-side
* **Finalize**: no lane_log overwrite, only status fields
* **Stale**: heartbeat based + UI can reset

That’s the right scalable design.

### AI  ``

### Solid, non‑manual solution

To make this robust and avoid manual field edits, the behavior should be:

1. **Reset button becomes a true “Stop + Clear” for dead runs**
   - When you press **Reset** on a lane that is `Requested` / `Running` / `AbortRequested`:
     - ERP **still asks** the connector to abort.
     - **But** after that, the server immediately clears that lane’s state in DB:
       - `lane_action_status = ""`
       - `lane_status = "Pending"`
       - `abort_requested = 0`
       - `run_id = ""`
       - live fields + logs cleared.
   - That way, even if the connector is dead, the ERP side lane is guaranteed to end in a **clean idle** state after Reset, and Upload checks will no longer be blocked by `AbortRequested`.

2. **Upload guard stays simple**
   - Upload only allowed when:
     - `lane_action_status == "Done"` (normal case), OR
     - `lane_action_status == ""` but `lane_status == "Completed"` (if you reset after a clean Done).
   - Upload **always blocked** when state is any of: `Requested`, `Running`, `AbortRequested`.

### AI  ``

Here is how **Google Sheets** is used in **`ERP_PTS-1.py`** only (this file; no other GSheet calls in the snippets we traced). `generate_unique_serial()` exists but is **never called** — it does not affect runtime.

---

### Target

- **Workbook:** `SPREADSHEET_ID` (`1BjubTA…`)
- **Tab:** **`.sheet1`** only — the **leftmost** tab (your screenshot **“Sheet1”** is correct).
- **Column A:** serial key used by the script  
- **Column B:** Bluetooth MAC

---

### If serial **and** MAC are **already** on the same row

**MAC update path** (`extract_mac_and_update_sheet`):

1. It finds the **first** row where column A **equals** `ser_no` (exact string match).
2. It writes **`update_cell(row, 2, mac_address)`** → **only column B on that row** is set again.

So:

- **Same serial, same MAC** → it **updates** B again with the same value (harmless / idempotent).
- **Same serial, new MAC** (e.g. different module) → it **overwrites** B with the new MAC.
- It **does not** insert a **new** row for MAC-only updates.

**Duplicate-MAC rule:** before writing, it scans pairs (A, B). If this MAC already appears on **another** row whose serial is **different** from `ser_no`, it **refuses** to write and returns **FAILED** (`[MAC DUPLICATE BLOCKED]`).

---

### All GSheet cases in this ERP script

| When | What happens to **column A** | What happens to **column B** |
|------|------------------------------|------------------------------|
| **Dump (`Fw_get`), normal, first time** | If `base` serial is **not** in A → **append** one new row: **A only** (`base`), B empty | Unchanged until dump+MAC step |
| **Dump (`Fw_get`), normal, serial already in A** | **No** new row; log: “already in sheet” | Unchanged until MAC step |
| **Dump (`Fw_get`), repaired** | **Always append** a new row: **A** = `config_serial` (e.g. `…_repaired` / `…_repaired_1`) | Unchanged until MAC step |
| **After successful dump** | No further A changes here | `extract_mac_and_update_sheet(config_serial)` → **update** B on row where A == `config_serial`, or **FAIL** if A missing / duplicate MAC on another SN |
| **After successful flash** (Mac Writing OK) | No change | Same function: **update** B for row where A == `config_serial` |

**Important details**

- **New rows** are created only in **`Fw_get`**, and only in **A** (never “MAC-only append”).
- **`extract_mac_and_update_sheet` never appends**; it only **`update_cell` on an existing A match** or fails.
- If the same serial appears **twice** in A, **`.index(ser_no)`** updates the **first** match only.
- **`generate_unique_serial`** is **unused** in the current file.

---

### Mismatch with “I thought it always appends”

Appending happens when the dump path **adds a new serial** to A (new base, or repaired variant). **MAC** for an existing serial is always **in-place update** of B, not a new row — which matches your sheet layout (one row per serial).

---

### Operational checklist

1. **`ERP_PTS-1_COPY.py` on the PC** should match this logic (same `SPREADSHEET_ID`, same tab = first sheet).  
2. **`ser_no` passed into MAC update** must match **exactly** the cell in A (`config_serial` can be `base` or `base_repaired_…` for repaired dumps).  
3. Confirm **`last_heartbeat_at`** on the lane child in ERPNext so the UI does not show false “connector offline” when the worker is actually running.

If you want, we can next add an optional log line that prints **before/after** B for that row (read cell after update) so operators see proof in the console.

### AI  ``

### Why this happened (how it’s possible)

From your logs:

- Lane 4 (SN `...0655`) dump+flash show:  
  `mac=DC:0D:30:5A:84:84`
- Lane 3 (SN `...0939`) dump+flash also show:  
  `mac=DC:0D:30:5A:84:84`

That means: **both dump operations read the same MAC from the same physical chip** at the moment of dump. Your code does:

- For each dump, it connects to **one COM port** and reads the MAC from the DUT via the `*_config.htf` file.
- Whatever MAC is inside that chip / HTF at that moment is:
  - Extracted by `update_file(config_serial)`
  - Burned during Mac Writing
  - Logged to ERP and to Google Sheet.

So if:

- The same USB COM port / relay channel was effectively connected to the **same physical PCB** when you dumped both `...0939` and `...0655`, or
- The wrong board was on that COM when you ran the second dump,

then both dumps are really talking to the **same chip**, so you really did burn and read the **same MAC** twice. The software doesn’t know it’s “a different board”; it only trusts “COM 107” and dumps whatever is physically there.

That’s why you see:

- Same COM shown in UI,
- Same MAC extracted,
- Same MAC logged for two different serials.

You haven’t lost the MAC value (it’s `DC:0D:30:5A:84:84`), but you **can’t know for sure which physical PCB has it now** because it was written twice.

---

If you want, next step we can do is:

- Add **hard guards in PTS1** so:
  - No two lanes can Run/Queue on the same COM at the same time.
  - Before writing a MAC to Google Sheets, we check if that MAC is already used by another serial and warn/block.

### AI  ``

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
History lines only got `|mac=...` when `mac` was non-empty (`if mac:`), so failed runs often had **no MAC** in `lane_result_json` even though ERP sometimes already had `mac_id` on the lane.

### Changes

**1. Server script — `record_lane_run`**
- Renamed payload MAC to `mac_from_payload`; still updates **`res.mac_id`** only when the connector sends a MAC.
- Builds **`line_mac`** for the history line in this order:  
  **connector payload → existing PTS1 Lane Result `mac_id` → parent PTS1 Test lane row `mac_id`**.
- **Always** appends **`|mac=`** to the line (value can be empty if nothing is known yet).
- Response **`mac_id`** in `out` now uses **`line_mac`** (fixed a bug where it still referenced removed `mac`).

**2. Server script — `upload_result_to_master_ledger`**
- Appends **`|mac=`** + resolved **`mac`** to the upload history entry (same style as run lines).

**3. PTS1 Station Connector**
- Before **`record_lane_run`**, if **`mac_seen`** is still empty after log parsing, it **reads `mac_id` from the current ERP lane** and sends that as **`mac_id`** so failures still record the last known MAC when ERP already has it.

### Example line shape
```text
ts=...|pts1_test=PTS1_testing_form|lane=4|op=flash|rc=1|status=Fail|msg=FLASH FAILED (rc=1)|mac=DC:0D:30:12:34:56
ts=...|pts1_test=PTS1_testing_form|lane=4|op=flash|rc=0|status=Pass|msg=FLASH SUCCESS (rc=0)|mac=DC:0D:30:12:34:56
```

**Deploy:** paste the updated **Server Script** into ERPNext and replace **PTS1 Station Connector** on the station PC.

Perfect — your **server script is already updated correctly** (✅ `missing_run_id` guard + ✅ `append_lane_log` logic + ✅ `reset_lane` clears run_id/connector_name/heartbeat).
Your **connector** also looks updated (✅ `patch_lane_mac(..., run_id)` + ✅ COM update sends run_id).

Now you asked again: **“give block to remove and block to paste”** — so here are the **ONLY remaining blocks** I would still change (small but important hardening). These are based on the exact code you pasted.

---

# 1) CONNECTOR — Heartbeat should ALWAYS include run_id (your code already does) ✅

But you are doing *two requests back-to-back* and printing `[HEARTBEAT NACK]`. Keep it, but fix one issue:

### Problem

If the server returns `{"ok": False, "reason": "missing_run_id"}` once, you retry with same payload (good).
But if server returns **run_id_mismatch** (rare), retrying is useless; you must **refresh run_id from ERP** once.

## ✅ REMOVE this whole “if not hb_ok” retry block

Find this part in connector inside `run_lane_job` heartbeat section:

```python
if not hb_ok:
    try:
        time.sleep(0.2)
        r = call_pts1_api({"api_cmd": "update_lane_fields", "docname": docname, "lane_no": lane_no, "fields": hb_fields}, timeout=20)
        msg = r.json().get("message") if isinstance(r.json().get("message"), dict) else {}
        hb_ok = msg.get("ok") is True
    except Exception as e2:
        print("[HEARTBEAT FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e2))
    if not hb_ok:
        print("[HEARTBEAT NACK]", docname, lane_no, msg)
```

## ✅ PASTE this improved block instead

```python
if not hb_ok:
    # If run_id mismatch, refresh run_id once from ERP and retry
    try:
        if isinstance(msg, dict) and msg.get("reason") == "run_id_mismatch":
            d2 = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
            r2 = find_lane_row(d2, lane_no) if d2 else None
            new_rid = safe_str(r2.get("run_id")) if r2 else ""
            if new_rid and new_rid != run_id:
                run_id = new_rid
                fields_base = {"run_id": run_id}
                hb_fields = dict(fields_base)
                hb_fields["lane_progress"] = 50
                hb_fields["last_heartbeat_at"] = 1
                hb_fields["lane_action_status"] = "Running"
                hb_fields["lane_status"] = "Running"
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Retry once
    try:
        time.sleep(0.2)
        r = call_pts1_api({"api_cmd": "update_lane_fields", "docname": docname, "lane_no": lane_no, "fields": hb_fields}, timeout=20)
        msg = r.json().get("message") if isinstance(r.json().get("message"), dict) else {}
        hb_ok = msg.get("ok") is True
    except Exception as e2:
        print("[HEARTBEAT FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e2))

    if not hb_ok:
        print("[HEARTBEAT NACK]", docname, lane_no, msg)
```

---

# 2) SERVER — claim_lane should NOT overwrite existing run_id (small safety)

Right now your server `claim_lane` **always sets run_id if connector sends it**, even if a run_id already exists. That can create mismatch in rare races.

## ✅ REMOVE this block inside `claim_lane`

```python
if run_id:
    try:
        frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id", run_id, update_modified=False)
    except Exception:
        pass
effective_run_id = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id") or "").strip() or run_id
```

## ✅ PASTE this safer block

```python
# Only set run_id if empty (server is source of truth)
if run_id and not cur_run_id:
    try:
        frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id", run_id, update_modified=False)
    except Exception:
        pass

effective_run_id = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id") or "").strip() or cur_run_id or run_id
```

# 3) CLIENT — Stop button is calling abort_lane with wrong arg name sometimes

In your client you call abort like this:

```js
args: { api_cmd: "abort_lane", docname: frm.doc.name, lane_no: lane_no }
```

## Fix: Serial cleared in lanes 2, 3, 4 after Enter

### Root cause

1. **Value lost before blur** – On Enter, the grid can clear or reset the cell before the blur handler runs.
2. **Order of updates** – Clearing the lane before setting the serial could overwrite the value.
3. **Refresh timing** – Refreshing the grid too early could read stale data.

### Changes made

1. **Capture value on Enter before blur**
   - On Enter, read the value from the input and store it in `frm.__pts1_enter_captured`.
   - Blur handler uses this stored value first, then DOM, then model.

2. **Update order**
   - Set `pcb_serial_no` first.
   - Then clear other lane fields.
   - Ensures the serial is in the model before any refresh.

3. **Deferred refresh**
   - Call `refresh_field("lanes")` inside `setTimeout(0)` so the model is updated before the grid re-renders.

4. **Error handling**
   - If the API call fails, show a message and do not reload.

5. **Captured value cleanup**
   - Clear the captured value only when it is used for the matching row.

You’re still hitting `_unpack_sequence_` because **RestrictedPython also forbids tuple “unpacking assignment”**, not just `for a, b in …`.

In our script we still had patterns like:

- `fs, fm = fc_fallback_get(docname)`
- `fc_st, fc_msg = read_find_com_merged(docname, doc)`

Those trigger `_unpack_sequence_` too, and that’s why `get_status_snapshot` was crashing.

### Fix applied (in `pts api server script 02-03-2026 - Copy.py`)
- **`fc_fallback_get()`** now returns a **dict**: `{"st": ..., "msg": ...}` (no tuple).
- **`read_find_com_merged()`** now returns a **dict**: `{"st": ..., "msg": ...}` (no tuple).
- **`peek_find_com_state`** and **`get_status_snapshot`** now read:

- `fc = read_find_com_merged(...)`
- `fc_st = fc.get("st")`
- `fc_msg = fc.get("msg")`

So there is **zero tuple unpacking** left.

Frappe **Server Scripts** run under **RestrictedPython**. Names that **start with `_`** (including **`def _fc_gkey`**, **`def _fc_fallback_set`**, etc.) are **rejected at compile time**. The script never loaded, so **every** `pts1_api` call (including **`reset_lane`**) failed with that `SyntaxError` — it wasn’t a bug in reset logic itself.

| `_fc_fallback_set` | `fc_fallback_set` |
| `_fc_fallback_clear_doc` | `fc_fallback_clear_doc` |
| `_fc_fallback_get` | `fc_fallback_get` |

## Fixes applied

### 1. **TimestampMismatchError (417)**

**Cause:** The PTS1 connector updates the document (lane status, logs, COM ports) while the client keeps an older copy. Autosave then tries to save that stale copy and Frappe rejects it.

**Change:** Serial changes now use the `update_lane_fields` API instead of a full form save. That API loads the document on the server and updates only the lane, so there is no timestamp conflict.

- **Serial entered/cleared** → `save_lane_via_api()` → `update_lane_fields` → reload form
- **Other changes** (e.g. Repaired PCB) → `debounced_autosave()` → on error, reload and show a message

- `sheet.update([[config_serial]], range_name=f"A{next_row}")`
- `sheet.update([[base]], range_name=f"A{next_row}")`

- Added `fw_file` to the allowed fields in `update_lane_fields`.

4. Server loads the document, updates lane 2, and saves.
5. Form reloads with the latest data (including connector updates).

   The connector reads this line and updates the lane’s `mac_id` in ERPNext.

5. **Updates Google Sheets**

### High‑level picture

You already have a clean architecture:

- **Client (`pts1 client script.js`)**: ERPNext form UI for `PTS1 Test` – 4 lanes, buttons for Dump/Flash/Upload/Reset, auto‑refresh, auto‑reset on serial change, COM‑scan helpers.
- **Server (`pts1_api` script)**: RestrictedPython API router handling `api_cmd` values (`update_lane_fields`, `record_lane_run`, `upload_result_to_master_ledger`, etc.), enforcing lifecycle/stage guardrails and updating `PTS1 Lane Result`, `PCB Master`, and `PCB Ledger`.
- **Connector (`PTS1 Station Connector.py`)**: Runs on the PTS PC. Polls ERPNext for jobs for this PC, auto‑runs `com_scan_headless.py` to assign COM ports, launches `ERP_PTS-1.py` per requested lane, streams logs, extracts MAC, updates lane state atomically via `update_lane_fields`, and calls `record_lane_run` once per dump/flash.

Key constraints from your spec are already enforced:

- **No bulk child-table overwrite from connector**: it *never* patches `lanes` directly, only uses `api_cmd="update_lane_fields"` per lane (also for auto COM updates and MAC patch).
- **MAC handling**: connector extracts MAC live from `ERP_PTS-1.py` output and patches `lane.mac_id` immediately; fallback parses the final chunk. Upload prefers lane MAC and falls back to `PTS1 Lane Result`.
- **record_lane_run**: is a robust UPSERT keyed by serial (`frappe.db.exists` + new_doc) and maintains counts, statuses, timestamps, and a bounded history string.
- **upload_result_to_master_ledger**: idempotent marker (`uploaded=1; uploaded_run_id=...`), re‑applies updates without throwing; checks that PCB is in PTS testing, computes `pts1_status` and `overall_status`, updates both Master and Ledger and UPSERTs `PTS1 Lane Result` with current lane fields and bounded history, then marks the lane JSON.
- **HTTP behavior**: connector treats HTTP 200 from `pts1_api` as success.
- **No duplicated connector helpers**: there's a single `call_pts1_api`, shared by `lane_update`, `patch_lane_mac`, and COM updates.

One minor note: the **COM scan status fields** (`find_com_status` / `find_com_message`) are currently only written by `api_cmd="request_find_com"` / `"update_find_com_result"` and not by the connector’s auto COM scan, so your “COM Assigned” hint in the client relies on the older `update_find_com_result` flow. Functionally, COM assignment still works via `update_lane_fields`, but the *status* fields won’t flip to `"Done"` unless you wire something to call `update_find_com_result`.

Below are the three full current versions (which already satisfy your listed rules A–H and the MAC/UPSERT/idempotency requirements).

### PTS1 Station Connector.py

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

"""
PTS1 Station Connector (Multi-lane, parallel) + AUTO COM SCAN

What it does:
- Poll ERPNext for PTS1 Test documents assigned to this PC (target_pc == hostname)
- Background runs com_scan_headless.py and writes COM ports into lanes (1..4)
- For each doc, finds lanes 1..4 where lane_action_status == "Requested"
- Starts each requested lane in parallel (up to MAX_PARALLEL_LANES)
- Claims the lane by patching lane_action_status -> Running before executing
- Streams ERP_PTS-1.py output into lane_log with throttled updates
- Finalizes lane_status + lane_action_status + lane_action_message + lane_progress
- Marks parent test_status Running/Completed/Failed smartly
"""

import os
import sys
import time
import json
import socket
import subprocess
import urllib.parse
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import requests


import re
MAC_RE = re.compile(r"Extracted Bluetooth MAC Address:\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]{2}(?::[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}){5})")

def extract_mac(text: str) -> str:
    if not text:
        return ""
    m = MAC_RE.search(text)
    if not m:
        return ""
    return (m.group(1) or "").strip().upper()


def call_pts1_api(args: dict, timeout=20):
    r = requests.post(
        urljoin("api/method/pts1_api"),
        headers=HEADERS,
        json=args,
        timeout=timeout
    )
    # ERPNext server scripts often return 200 only
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise RuntimeError("pts1_api HTTP " + str(r.status_code) + " " + (r.text or "")[:300])
    return r


def lane_update(docname: str, lane_no: int, fields: dict):
    # atomic, lane-only update (no overwriting other lanes)
    call_pts1_api(
        {
            "api_cmd": "update_lane_fields",
            "docname": docname,
            "lane_no": lane_no,
            "fields": fields
        },
        timeout=20
    )

def patch_lane_mac(docname: str, lane_no: int, mac: str):
    if not mac:
        return
    mac = str(mac).strip().upper()
    if not mac:
        return

    try:
        # avoid extra writes if already set
        d = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
        if d:
            row = find_lane_row(d, lane_no)
            if row:
                cur = safe_str(row.get("mac_id")).strip().upper()
                if cur == mac:
                    return

        lane_update(docname, lane_no, {"mac_id": mac})
    except Exception as e:
        print("[MAC PATCH FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))

def auto_update_com_ports_for_doc(docname: str, ports: list):
    if not ports:
        return

    doc = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
    if not doc:
        return

    changed_any = False

    for lane_no in range(1, COM_ASSIGN_MAX + 1):
        row = find_lane_row(doc, lane_no)
        if not row:
            continue

        if not lane_idle_for_com_update(row):
            continue

        cur = safe_str(row.get("com_port"))
        newv = ports[lane_no - 1] if (lane_no - 1) < len(ports) else ""
        newv = safe_str(newv)

        if not newv:
            continue

        if COM_ONLY_IF_EMPTY and cur:
            continue

        if cur != newv:
            try:
                lane_update(docname, lane_no, {"com_port": newv})
                changed_any = True
            except Exception as e:
                print("[COM UPDATE FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))

    if changed_any:
        print("[COM UPDATED]", docname, ports)


# ==========================
# CONFIG (edit only these)
# ==========================
ERP_URL = "http://192.168.1.50:8080/"   # MUST end with /
API_KEY = "95403196454d1c9"
API_SECRET = "eac4a78c7ddafa8"

DOCTYPE_PARENT = "PTS1 Test"
CHILD_FIELD = "lanes"

POLL_SEC = 1.0

# MUST be the python that can run ERP_PTS-1.py (has yaml, gspread etc.)
PYTHON_EXE = sys.executable

# Your runner program
PTS1_SCRIPT = r"D:\PTS_1\PTS_1\ERP_PTS-1.py"

# COM scan script
COMSCAN_SCRIPT = r"D:\PTS_1\PTS_1\com_scan_headless.py"

# Parallel lanes
MAX_PARALLEL_LANES = 4

# How often to push logs to ERP
LOG_PUSH_SEC = 3.0

# Limit log size kept in ERP
LOG_KEEP_CHARS = 15000

# Retry patch attempts
PATCH_RETRIES = 3
PATCH_RETRY_SLEEP = 0.8

# ---------- AUTO COM SCAN ----------
COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC = 2.0     # scan every N seconds
COM_ASSIGN_MAX = 4              # lanes 1..4
COM_ONLY_IF_EMPTY = True        # do not overwrite existing com_port
COM_UPDATE_ONLY_WHEN_IDLE = True  # only update com when lane_action_status is empty/Done (safer)

# Action mapping (ERP -> operation)
ACTION_TO_OP = {
    "VERIFY": "dump",   # VERIFY means DUMP
    "DUMP": "dump",
    "FLASH": "flash"
}


# ==========================
# HTTP setup
# ==========================
HEADERS = {
    "Authorization": f"token {API_KEY}:{API_SECRET}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
}

PC_NAME = socket.gethostname()


# ==========================
# Helpers
# ==========================
def urljoin(path: str) -> str:
    return ERP_URL.rstrip("/") + "/" + path.lstrip("/")


def erp_get(path: str, params=None, timeout=30):
    return requests.get(urljoin(path), headers=HEADERS, params=params, timeout=timeout)


def erp_put(path: str, data: dict, timeout=30):
    return requests.put(urljoin(path), headers=HEADERS, data=json.dumps(data), timeout=timeout)

def safe_str(x):
    return "" if x is None else str(x).strip()


def patch_doc(doctype: str, name: str, fields: dict):
    r = erp_put(
        f"api/resource/{urllib.parse.quote(doctype)}/{urllib.parse.quote(name)}",
        fields,
        timeout=30
    )
    return r


def patch_ok(doctype: str, name: str, fields: dict, label: str = "") -> bool:
    for i in range(PATCH_RETRIES):
        try:
            r = patch_doc(doctype, name, fields)
            if r.status_code == 200:
                return True
            print(f"[ERP PATCH FAIL]{' '+label if label else ''}", r.status_code, r.text[:350])
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[ERP PATCH EXC]{' '+label if label else ''}", repr(e))
        time.sleep(PATCH_RETRY_SLEEP * (i + 1))
    return False


def get_doc(doctype: str, name: str):
    r = erp_get(f"api/resource/{urllib.parse.quote(doctype)}/{urllib.parse.quote(name)}", timeout=30)
    if r.status_code != 200:
        print("[ERP GET FAIL]", r.status_code, r.text[:350])
        return None
    return r.json()["data"]


def list_jobs_for_pc():
    fields = json.dumps(["name", "target_pc", "test_status", "modified"])
    filters = json.dumps([
        [DOCTYPE_PARENT, "target_pc", "=", PC_NAME]
    ])
    params = {
        "fields": fields,
        "filters": filters,
        "order_by": "modified desc",
        "limit_page_length": 20
    }
    r = erp_get(f"api/resource/{urllib.parse.quote(DOCTYPE_PARENT)}", params=params, timeout=30)
    if r.status_code != 200:
        print("[LIST FAIL]", r.status_code, r.text[:350])
        return []
    return r.json().get("data", [])


def find_lane_row(doc, lane_no: int):
    lanes = doc.get(CHILD_FIELD, []) or []
    for row in lanes:
        try:
            if int(row.get("lane_no") or 0) == int(lane_no):
                return row
        except Exception:
            pass
    for row in lanes:
        if safe_str(row.get("lane_no")) == str(lane_no):
            return row
    return None


def run_pts1(slot: int, op: str, serial: str, comport: str):
    cmd = [
        PYTHON_EXE,
        PTS1_SCRIPT,
        "--slot", str(slot),
        "--operation", op,
        "--serial", serial,
        "--comport", comport
    ]
    print("[RUN]", " ".join(cmd))

    p = subprocess.Popen(
        cmd,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
        bufsize=1,
        universal_newlines=True,
        cwd=os.path.dirname(PTS1_SCRIPT) or None
    )
    return p


# ==========================
# AUTO COM SCAN
# ==========================
def run_com_scan():
    """
    Runs com_scan_headless.py and returns list like ["112","106","114","107"]
    """
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(
            [PYTHON_EXE, "-u", COMSCAN_SCRIPT],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30
        )
        out = (p.stdout or "").strip()
        if not out:
            return []
        data = json.loads(out)
        if data.get("ok"):
            ports = data.get("ports") or []
            return [str(x).strip() for x in ports if str(x).strip()]
    except Exception as e:
        print("[COMSCAN ERROR]", repr(e))
    return []


def lane_idle_for_com_update(row: dict) -> bool:
    if not COM_UPDATE_ONLY_WHEN_IDLE:
        return True
    st = safe_str(row.get("lane_action_status")).lower()
    # allow update when not running/requested
    return (st == "" or st == "done")




# ==========================
# Parallel lane runner
# ==========================
EXECUTOR = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=MAX_PARALLEL_LANES)
IN_FLIGHT = set()
IN_FLIGHT_LOCK = threading.Lock()


def mark_parent_running(docname: str):
    patch_ok(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname, {"test_status": "Running"}, label="parent->Running")


def finalize_parent_if_idle(docname: str):
    d = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
    if not d:
        return

    lanes = d.get(CHILD_FIELD, []) or []
    active = any(safe_str(x.get("lane_action_status")).lower() in ("requested", "running") for x in lanes)
    if active:
        return

    any_failed = any(safe_str(x.get("lane_status")).lower() in ("failed", "aborted") for x in lanes)
    parent_status = "Failed" if any_failed else "Completed"
    patch_ok(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname, {"test_status": parent_status}, label=f"parent->{parent_status}")

def run_lane_job(docname: str, lane_no: int):
    key = (docname, lane_no)
    try:
        doc = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
        if not doc:
            return

        row = find_lane_row(doc, lane_no)
        if not row:
            print(f"[SKIP] {docname}: lane {lane_no} row not found")
            return

        action = safe_str(row.get("lane_action"))
        action_status = safe_str(row.get("lane_action_status"))
        pcb_serial = safe_str(row.get("pcb_serial_no"))
        comport = safe_str(row.get("com_port"))

        print(f"[DOC] {docname} lane{lane_no} action={action} a_status={action_status} serial={pcb_serial} com={comport}")

        if action_status.lower() != "requested":
            return

        op = ACTION_TO_OP.get(action.upper())
        if not op:
            try:
                lane_update(docname, lane_no, {
                    "lane_status": "Failed",
                    "lane_action_status": "Done",
                    "lane_action_message": "Unknown action: " + action,
                    "lane_progress": 100
                })
            except Exception as e:
                print("[UNKNOWN ACTION UPDATE FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))

            finalize_parent_if_idle(docname)
            return

        if not pcb_serial or not comport:
            try:
                lane_update(docname, lane_no, {
                    "lane_status": "Failed",
                    "lane_action_status": "Done",
                    "lane_action_message": "Missing PCB Serial No or COM Port",
                    "lane_progress": 100
                })
            except Exception as e:
                print("[MISSING FIELDS UPDATE FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))

            finalize_parent_if_idle(docname)
            return

        # CLAIM lane (atomic)
        try:
            lane_update(docname, lane_no, {
                "lane_status": "Running",
                "lane_action_status": "Running",
                "lane_action_message": op.upper() + " Running",
                "lane_progress": 1,
                "lane_log": ""
            })
        except Exception as e:
            print("[CLAIM FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))
            return

        mark_parent_running(docname)

        # RUN
        p = run_pts1(lane_no, op, pcb_serial, comport)

        log_cache = ""
        last_push = 0.0
        mac_seen = ""

        for line in iter(p.stdout.readline, ""):
            if not line:
                break

            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            print(f"[PTS1 L{lane_no}]", line)

            log_cache += line + "\n"

            m = extract_mac(line)
            if m and m != mac_seen:
                mac_seen = m
                print(f"[MAC] lane{lane_no} {pcb_serial} -> {mac_seen}")
                patch_lane_mac(docname, lane_no, mac_seen)

            now = time.time()
            if now - last_push > LOG_PUSH_SEC:
                last_push = now

                # merge with latest lane_log from server (avoid overwriting)
                d3 = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
                if not d3:
                    continue

                r3 = find_lane_row(d3, lane_no)
                existing = safe_str(r3.get("lane_log")) if r3 else ""
                merged = (existing + log_cache)[-LOG_KEEP_CHARS:]

                try:
                    lane_update(docname, lane_no, {
                        "lane_log": merged,
                        "lane_progress": 50
                    })
                except Exception as e:
                    print("[LOGPUSH FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))

                log_cache = ""

        rc = p.wait()

        # MAC fallback from last chunk
        if not mac_seen:
            mac_seen = extract_mac(log_cache)
            if mac_seen:
                patch_lane_mac(docname, lane_no, mac_seen)

        passed = (rc == 0)
        final_lane_status = "Completed" if passed else "Failed"
        msg = op.upper() + (" SUCCESS (rc=0)" if passed else (" FAILED (rc=" + str(rc) + ")"))

        # Record run ONCE (dump/flash stats)
        try:
            call_pts1_api({
                "api_cmd": "record_lane_run",
                "docname": docname,
                "lane_no": lane_no,
                "serial": pcb_serial,
                "op": op,
                "rc": rc,
                "message": msg,
                "mac_id": mac_seen
            }, timeout=20)
        except Exception as e:
            print("[record_lane_run FAIL]", repr(e))

        print(f"[DONE] {docname} lane{lane_no} op={op} exit={rc}")

        # finalize lane (atomic)
        d4 = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
        if not d4:
            return
        r4 = find_lane_row(d4, lane_no)
        existing = safe_str(r4.get("lane_log")) if r4 else ""
        final_log = (existing + log_cache)[-LOG_KEEP_CHARS:]

        try:
            lane_update(docname, lane_no, {
                "lane_status": final_lane_status,
                "lane_action_status": "Done",
                "lane_action_message": msg,
                "lane_progress": 100,
                "lane_log": final_log
            })
        except Exception as e:
            print("[FINALIZE FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))

        finalize_parent_if_idle(docname)

    except Exception as e:
        print("[LANE JOB ERROR]", docname, lane_no, repr(e))
        try:
            lane_update(docname, lane_no, {
                "lane_status": "Failed",
                "lane_action_status": "Done",
                "lane_action_message": "Connector exception: " + repr(e),
                "lane_progress": 100
            })
        except Exception as e2:
            print("[EXCEPTION UPDATE FAIL]", docname, lane_no, repr(e2))

        finalize_parent_if_idle(docname)

    finally:
        with IN_FLIGHT_LOCK:
            IN_FLIGHT.discard(key)

def process_doc(docname: str):
    doc = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
    if not doc:
        return

    lanes = doc.get(CHILD_FIELD, []) or []
    requested = []
    for r in lanes:
        try:
            lane_no = int(r.get("lane_no") or 0)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if lane_no < 1 or lane_no > 4:
            continue
        if safe_str(r.get("lane_action_status")).lower() == "requested":
            requested.append(lane_no)

    if not requested:
        return

    for lane_no in requested:
        key = (docname, lane_no)
        with IN_FLIGHT_LOCK:
            if key in IN_FLIGHT:
                continue
            if len(IN_FLIGHT) >= MAX_PARALLEL_LANES:
                break
            IN_FLIGHT.add(key)

        EXECUTOR.submit(run_lane_job, docname, lane_no)


# ==========================
# Startup checks
# ==========================
def startup_checks():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("PTS1 Station Connector starting (MULTI-LANE + AUTO COM)")
    print("ERP_URL   =", ERP_URL)
    print("PC_NAME   =", PC_NAME)
    print("PYTHON    =", PYTHON_EXE)
    print("SCRIPT    =", PTS1_SCRIPT)
    print("COMSCAN   =", COMSCAN_SCRIPT)
    print("PARALLEL  =", MAX_PARALLEL_LANES)
    print("POLL_SEC  =", POLL_SEC)
    print("LOG_PUSH  =", LOG_PUSH_SEC)
    print("COM_SCAN_INTERVAL =", COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC)
    print("COM_ONLY_IF_EMPTY =", COM_ONLY_IF_EMPTY)
    print("COM_UPDATE_ONLY_WHEN_IDLE =", COM_UPDATE_ONLY_WHEN_IDLE)
    print("=" * 60)

    r = erp_get("api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user", timeout=30)
    if r.status_code != 200:
        print("Auth FAIL:", r.status_code, r.text[:300])
        sys.exit(2)
    print("Auth OK as:", r.json().get("message"))

    r2 = erp_get("api/resource/PTS1%20Test?limit_page_length=1", timeout=30)
    if r2.status_code != 200:
        print("PTS1 Test NOT reachable:", r2.status_code, r2.text[:300])
        sys.exit(3)
    print("PTS1 Test reachable; sample:", r2.json().get("data"))

    # quick com scan sanity
    ports = run_com_scan()
    print("[COMSCAN TEST] ports =", ports)


# ==========================
# Main loop
# ==========================
def main():
    startup_checks()

    last_com_scan = 0.0
    last_ports = []

    while True:
        try:
            jobs = list_jobs_for_pc()

            # background COM scan
            now = time.time()
            if now - last_com_scan >= COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC:
                last_com_scan = now
                ports = run_com_scan()
                if ports and ports != last_ports:
                    last_ports = ports
                    for j in jobs:
                        auto_update_com_ports_for_doc(j["name"], ports)

            # normal lane processing
            for j in jobs:
                process_doc(j["name"])

        except Exception as e:
            print("[LOOP ERROR]", repr(e))

        time.sleep(POLL_SEC)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
