### What this error means

MySQL error **1054 Unknown column `find_com_status`** means the table **`tabPTS1 Test`** still has **no** columns for those fields. Until they exist, **Find COM cannot work** — the Server Script has to write `find_com_status` / `find_com_message` on the parent document.

**417 EXPECTATION FAILED** is normal in Frappe when the server raises **ValidationError** (`frappe.throw`). It is not a separate “COM” failure.

### What you must do (one time per site)

1. **Customize Form → PTS1 Test**  
   Add:
   - `find_com_status` — **Data**  
   - `find_com_message` — **Small Text** (or **Text**)

2. **Save** the DocType.

3. On the **same machine / bench** that serves `192.168.1.50:8080`, run:

   ```bash
   bench migrate --site YOUR_ACTUAL_SITE_NAME
   ```

   Replace `YOUR_ACTUAL_SITE_NAME` with the site id (often in `sites/currentsite.txt` or your `common_site_config`).

4. Confirm:

   ```bash
   bench --site YOUR_ACTUAL_SITE_NAME mariadb -e "SHOW COLUMNS FROM \`tabPTS1 Test\` LIKE 'find_com%';"
   ```

   You should see **`find_com_status`** and **`find_com_message`**.

If you only use the UI and **never** run **`bench migrate`**, the columns will **never** appear and this error will continue.

### If Customize Form did not create columns

From **`bench console`** (same site):

```python
from frappe.custom.doctype.custom_field.custom_field import create_custom_fields

create_custom_fields({"PTS1 Test": [
    {"fieldname": "find_com_status", "label": "Find COM Status", "fieldtype": "Data", "insert_after": "target_pc"},
    {"fieldname": "find_com_message", "label": "Find COM Message", "fieldtype": "Small Text", "insert_after": "find_com_status"},
]})
frappe.db.commit()
frappe.clear_cache()
```

If that errors on **`insert_after`**, change **`target_pc`** to a field name that **really exists** on **PTS1 Test** (first field after which you want them to appear).

The same **bench console** recipe is now in the **comments at the top** of `pts api server script 02-03-2026 - Copy.py` in your project.

### UI text

The client script is updated so the dialog shows **either** the server’s ValidationError line **or** one short fallback — not two duplicated paragraphs. Sync the latest **`pts1 client script.js`** into ERPNext and reload (hard refresh / clear cache) so you get that behavior.

Until **`bench migrate`** (or the console `create_custom_fields` + commit) has run successfully, **Find COM** will keep failing with this message — that is expected.

### USER  ``

it’s not clearing because your current auto-reset hook only runs when the child row field event fires, and in many ERPNext grids it won’t fire reliably unless the row is properly “committed” (blur + model event). Also, some of your values (MAC + status) are already saved in DB, so they will keep showing until you explicitly blank them and save.

Do this simple, guaranteed fix:

✅ Fix (most reliable): clear lane when you leave the serial cell (grid blur)
1) In your client script, find your function:

setup_auto_reset_on_serial_change(frm)

2) REPLACE the entire function with this one:
function setup_auto_reset_on_serial_change(frm) {
  if (frm.__pts1_serial_reset_hooked) return;
  frm.__pts1_serial_reset_hooked = true;

  const KEEP_COM_ON_NEW_SERIAL = true;
  const KEEP_COM_ON_CLEAR = true; // recommended: keep fixed COM per lane

  function clear_lane_row(cdt, cdn, keep_com) {
    const fields = {
      lane_status: "Pending",
      lane_action: "",
      lane_action_status: "",
      lane_action_message: "",
      lane_progress: 0,
      lane_step: "",
      error_message: "",
      lane_log: "",
      mac_id: "",
      lane_result_json: "",
      fw_file: ""
    };
    if (!keep_com) fields.com_port = "";

    Object.keys(fields).forEach((k) => {
      frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, k, fields[k]);
    });
  }

  function debounced_autosave() {
    if (frm.__pts1_autosave_timer) clearTimeout(frm.__pts1_autosave_timer);
    frm.__pts1_autosave_timer = setTimeout(() => {
      frm.__pts1_autosave_timer = null;
      if (!frm.is_new() && frm.is_dirty()) frm.save().catch(() => {});
    }, 300);
  }

  // ✅ 1) Track old serial per row
  frm.__pts1_prev_serial_map = frm.__pts1_prev_serial_map || {};

  // ✅ 2) Hard hook on grid input blur (works even when frappe.model.on fails)
  const grid = frm.fields_dict.lanes?.grid;
  if (!grid?.wrapper) return;

  grid.wrapper.off("blur.pts1serial");
  grid.wrapper.on("blur.pts1serial", 'input[data-fieldname="pcb_serial_no"]', function () {
    const $inp = $(this);
    const cdn = $inp.closest(".grid-row").attr("data-name");
    if (!cdn) return;

    const row = locals[grid.doctype]?.[cdn];
    if (!row) return;

    const new_serial = (row.pcb_serial_no || "").toString().trim();
    const old_serial = (frm.__pts1_prev_serial_map[cdn] || "").toString().trim();

    // update tracker
    frm.__pts1_prev_serial_map[cdn] = new_serial;

    // Serial cleared -> clear lane
    if (!new_serial) {
      clear_lane_row(row.doctype, row.name, KEEP_COM_ON_CLEAR);
      frm.refresh_field("lanes");
      if (frm.fields_dict.lane_dashboard) render_lane_dashboard(frm);
      debounced_autosave();
      return;
    }

    // Serial changed -> clear lane (keep COM)
    if (new_serial !== old_serial) {
      clear_lane_row(row.doctype, row.name, KEEP_COM_ON_NEW_SERIAL);
      // restore serial after clearing
      frappe.model.set_value(row.doctype, row.name, "pcb_serial_no", new_serial);

      frm.refresh_field("lanes");
      if (frm.fields_dict.lane_dashboard) render_lane_dashboard(frm);
      debounced_autosave();
    }
  });
}
✅ Why this works

It does not depend on frappe.model.on(...) being triggered.

It hooks the actual input blur event in the grid.

It explicitly clears mac_id, lane_status, lane_action_status, logs, etc.

It autosaves so the cleared state persists

### USER  ``

Yes — **your changes are *conceptually* enough**, but there are **2 specific gaps** that will still cause the “manual reload needed” feeling even after rc/exit codes are fixed.

I’ll break it into 3 parts:

1. What your system is doing end-to-end (why you needed manual reload earlier)
2. What is already fixed by your current changes (worker_mode sys.exit + client polling snapshot)
3. The **exact final fixes** you must do in connector + client so ERP updates live with **zero manual reload** and **no “Refreshing…” button** confusion.

---

## 1) Why manual reload was needed earlier (root cause)

You had **two different issues mixed**:

### A) Connector did not have a reliable “PASS/FAIL” signal

* Your ERP_PTS-1.py previously exited with **0 always**
* So connector printed:
  `[DONE] ... exit=0` even when internal steps failed
* That caused ERP lane fields to not reflect failure properly (or stay “Running/Requested” in some cases if finalize wasn’t reached)

✅ You fixed this by adding `sys.exit(0/1)` based on PASSED/FAILED.

### B) UI was showing “Queued / Requested” until you reloaded

Even if connector updates the DB, **Frappe UI does NOT auto-refresh child table values** unless:

* you manually reload the doc, OR
* you pull snapshot and apply it into grid, OR
* you run reload_doc() (which you don’t want while typing)

✅ You are fixing this with `get_status_snapshot` polling + `apply_snapshot_to_grid`.

So **manual reload should no longer be required** *if your poll loop keeps running* and if it applies snapshot properly.

---

## 2) What you already have correct

### ✅ Connector finalization is correct

At the end of `run_lane_job()` you do:

```python
lane_update(docname, lane_no, {
  "lane_status": final_lane_status,
  "lane_action_status": "Done",
  "lane_action_message": msg,
  "lane_progress": 100,
  "lane_log": final_log,
  "repaired_pcb": repaired
})
```

That is correct. It updates ERP without any reload required.

### ✅ Client snapshot polling is correct **in design**

Your new functions:

* `poll_status_snapshot()`
* `apply_snapshot_to_grid()`
* `start_auto_refresh_if_needed()`

This is the correct architecture:

* **No reload_doc**
* **Only live runtime keys**
* **Skip updates while typing**
* **Refresh grid and dashboard**

So **YES** — this is the right direction.

---

## 3) What is still missing (and why you still see “Queued → Running → Completed only after manual reload”)

### Problem #1: Your polling stops when “Requested” is cleared too early or UI doesn’t detect active lanes

Your `start_auto_refresh_if_needed(frm)` decides if it should keep polling by checking:

```js
anyLaneActive(frm) || anyLaneActiveFromSnapshot(frm.__pts1_live)
```

But here’s the catch:

* At the moment you click Dump/Flash, you set local row to Requested.
* Connector immediately patches lane_action_status -> Running.
* Your snapshot poll must run quickly enough to catch it.
* If it doesn’t, and local state becomes “not requested/not running” due to model inconsistencies, **timer may not start** or may stop.

✅ You partially solved with `force_start_polling(frm, 12)`.

But you must ensure:

* `force_start_polling()` is called **every time** action is queued
* and your “auto refresh” stays alive until Done.

You already call it here:

```js
force_start_polling(frm, 12);
```

**But 12 seconds is sometimes not enough**, because your dump/flash takes longer than that.

So after 12 seconds, if `start_auto_refresh_if_needed` didn’t kick in properly, polling dies, and you need manual reload.

✅ Fix: make forced polling longer (or until status becomes Done).

**Do this:**

* `force_start_polling(frm, 120)` (2 minutes)
* OR better: keep forced polling until lane_action_status becomes Done for that lane.

---

### Problem #2: apply_snapshot_to_grid currently skips updates while typing (good) BUT also skips when focus stays inside grid wrapper even after test finishes

This can happen if:

* user clicked inside grid and cursor stays there
* your typing detection:

```js
$(ae).closest(".grid-row").length
```

will block snapshot apply forever until they click outside, so UI will “look stuck”.

✅ Fix: only block snapshot apply if the active input is actually in **pcb_serial_no** or **com_port** cell, not any focus inside grid.

Example safer typing detector:

```js
const typingNow =
  ae &&
  (ae.tagName === "INPUT" || ae.tagName === "TEXTAREA") &&
  (ae.getAttribute("data-fieldname") === "pcb_serial_no" || ae.getAttribute("data-fieldname") === "com_port");
```

This way, if user clicked somewhere else, snapshot still applies.

---

### Problem #3: You are not refreshing the **dashboard field** if it is based on snapshot only

You *are* calling:

```js
render_lane_dashboard(frm, msg);
```

So good.

But if your dashboard is the main view, and the child table refresh is blocked by typing, dashboard updates will still show correct status even when grid doesn’t.

So the fix is: allow dashboard refresh always, block only grid update.

Right now you block snapshot apply, but still call render_lane_dashboard — that is correct. Good.

---

## 4) Final recommended changes (minimal and solid)

### ✅ A) Change forced polling to 2 minutes (fast fix)

In request_action `.then()`:

```js
force_start_polling(frm, 12);
```

Change to:

```js
force_start_polling(frm, 120);
```

That alone will stop the “manual reload” symptom for long operations.

---

### ✅ B) Improve typing detection so grid updates aren’t blocked forever

Replace typing logic in `apply_snapshot_to_grid()`:

Current:

```js
const typingNow =
  ae &&
  (ae.tagName === "INPUT" || ae.tagName === "TEXTAREA") &&
  $(ae).closest(".grid-row").length;
if (typingNow) return;
```

Change to:

```js
const typingNow =
  ae &&
  (ae.tagName === "INPUT" || ae.tagName === "TEXTAREA") &&
  ["pcb_serial_no", "com_port"].includes(ae.getAttribute("data-fieldname") || "");
if (typingNow) return;
```

This keeps your “enter serial during test” feature, without freezing updates.

### ✅ C) Guarantee polling keeps running until all active lanes are Done

    if action != "VERIFY" and action != "FLASH":

    doc = get_pts_doc(docname)
    row = get_lane_row(doc, lane_no)

    # Child table doctype resolved dynamically (lanes table)
    child_dt = frappe.get_meta("PTS1 Test").get_field("lanes").options

    p_sn = (payload.get("pcb_serial_no") or "").strip()
    p_cp = (payload.get("com_port") or "").strip()

    # ✅ If payload is given, treat it as truth (prevents old serial/com being used)
    if p_sn:
        try:
            frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "pcb_serial_no", p_sn, update_modified=False)
        except Exception:
            pass
    if p_cp:
        try:
            frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "com_port", p_cp, update_modified=False)
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Re-read from DB (safe)
    serial_now = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, row.name, "pcb_serial_no") or "").strip()
    com_now = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, row.name, "com_port") or "").strip()

    if serial_now == "" or com_now == "":
        frappe.throw("Lane " + str(lane_no) + ": PCB Serial No and COM Port are required")

    # ✅ Queue action atomically for ONLY this lane
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "lane_action", action, update_modified=False)
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "lane_action_status", "Requested", update_modified=False)
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "lane_status", "Queued", update_modified=False)
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "lane_progress", 0, update_modified=False)
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "lane_action_message", "", update_modified=False)
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, row.name, "error_message", "", update_modified=False)

    # Parent status update (safe)
    try:
        frappe.db.set_value("PTS1 Test", docname, "test_status", "Queued", update_modified=False)
    except Exception:
        pass

    frappe.db.commit()
    out = {"ok": True, "api_cmd": api_cmd, "doc": docname, "lane": lane_no, "action": action}

   - When you press **Reset** on a lane that is `Requested` / `Running` / `AbortRequested`:

Here’s what was implemented and how it behaves.

### 1. **Dump / Flash (unchanged)**
- **PTS1 Station Connector** still runs the same CLI per lane/COM (`run_pts1` → `ERP_PTS-1.py` worker). No changes there, so dump/flash (including MAC handling in your tooling) stay as before.

### 2. **Stop (new orange button)**
- Calls **`abort_lane`** only.
- **Server `abort_lane`** (restored for the connector):
  - **`Requested`** → immediately **`Done` + `Aborted`** (“Stopped before run started”) so nothing is stuck if the job never claimed.
  - **`Running`** → **`AbortRequested` + `Aborting`** so the connector can see it, kill the subprocess, and finalize **`Done` + `Aborted`** (existing connector logic).
- **Stale**: **Stop is disabled**; message tells the operator to use **Reset** (station can’t see ERP).

### 3. **Reset (always labeled Reset)**
- **Idle**: **`reset_lane`** → clears **serial, MAC, logs, status, run_id, history fields, repaired_pcb on the row**, etc. **`com_port` is kept**.
- **Stale**: same full **`reset_lane`** (no Stop).
- **Busy (not stale)**: **`abort_lane` → wait until** `lane_action_status` is no longer `Requested` / `Running` / `AbortRequested` **→ `reset_lane`** (full wipe, COM kept).
- **Timeout (~2 min)**: second confirm offers **force ERP clear** (`force_clear=1`) so you’re not stuck; warning if tooling might still be running on the PC.

### 4. **`reset_lane` safety on the server**
- If the lane is still **`Requested` / `Running` / `AbortRequested`**, a plain **`reset_lane`** is **rejected** (avoids wiping while a run is active), unless **`force_clear`** is set (used only after the timeout path).

### 5. **Upload / “AbortRequested” on PTS1 Lane Result**
- When saving **PTS1 Lane Result**, **`lane_action_status`** is normalized to allowed options; anything else (e.g. **`AbortRequested`**) is stored as **`Done`**, so you should no longer get validation errors from that field during upload.

### AI  ``

### Short answer

What you described is basically how the connector behaves now, with a couple of switches that control safety.

### 1) Baseline COMs when connector starts

- On startup, the connector enters the main loop and immediately starts background scans every **`COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC`** seconds.
- Each scan calls **`com_scan_headless.py`**, which now returns:
  - `slots = [A,B,C,D]` → direct mapping for **lanes 1–4**
  - `ports = [...]` → older packed list, only used as fallback
- For each **PTS1 Test** document assigned to this PC, the connector runs:

```python
apply_auto_com_from_scan(docname, ports, slots)
```

- With `COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "slot"` this means:
  - `lane 1` gets `slots[0]`, `lane 2` gets `slots[1]`, etc.
  - Empty string clears COM for that lane.
- That is your **baseline for the session**: ERP lanes are populated from the current USB layout and stay that way unless a later scan detects a change.

(If you want an *extra* scan before the loop, set `COM_SCAN_AT_STARTUP = True`; it will run once with a short timeout.)

### 2) Continuous background scan (A/B/C/D)

- The main loop continues to call **`run_com_scan()`** every **`COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC`**.
- Each time, it recomputes `slots = [A,B,C,D]` and, when the signature changes, re-applies `apply_auto_com_from_scan` so ERP stays in sync.
- That satisfies **“com_scan_headless will continuously scan … and keeps ports in a,b,c,d format”**.

### 3) Per‑lane preflight before each Dump / Flash

Inside `run_lane_job` after we successfully **claim** the lane:

1. We call:

```python
effective_com, pre_err = resolve_com_preflight(docname, lane_no, comport, run_id)
```

2. `resolve_com_preflight` does:

- Runs **`run_com_scan()`** again (fresh) and computes **for this lane only**:

```python
scanned = scan_com_for_lane(lane_no, ports, slots)
```

- Compares **ERP `com_port` vs scanned** and follows this logic:

  - **Both set and equal** → OK, uses that COM.
  - **Both set but different**  
    - With **`COM_PREFLIGHT_TRUST_SCAN = True`** (your setting) it:
      - Writes the scanned COM back into ERP (`lane_update` with `run_id`)
      - Uses the scanned COM for CLI.
    - With it **False**, it fails the lane with a clear mismatch message.
  - **Scanned set, ERP empty** → writes scanned COM into ERP, then runs.
  - **Scan empty, ERP has COM**:
    - If **`COM_PREFLIGHT_ALLOW_ERP_IF_SCAN_EMPTY = False`** (current, safe), it **fails** the lane and tells you to fix USB / Find COM.
    - If set to **True**, it will **still run** using the ERP COM (risky, but available).

3. If `pre_err` is not empty, the lane is finalized as **Failed / Done** *before* starting `ERP_PTS‑1.py`, so no wrong DUT is flashed.

Only this **one lane** is checked; other lanes and ports are untouched during that preflight.

---

If you want an extra safety layer using a **session baseline** (first good `slots` scan) as a fallback when a later scan returns empty, we can add that next, but the current design already does:

- baseline COM → written to ERP via auto‑scan,
- continuous **A/B/C/D** scanning,
- and a **per‑lane COM confirmation** right before every Dump/Flash.

- Inside `update_file`, the emoji `✅` (and possibly `❌`) caused a **Unicode / charmap error** on Windows.
- That made `update_file` return `"FAILED"` (or raise), and your code does:

  ```python
  if update_ret == "PASSED":
      print("#####---- MAC extracted from dump HTF file ----####")
  else:
      print("#####---- MAC extraction/update FAILED ----####")
      test_return = "FAILED"
      test_log.append("MAC extraction/update FAILED")
  ```

- So **only because** `update_file` failed, `test_return` becomes `"FAILED"` and you see `Dump completed with status: FAILED`.

Now that we removed the emojis from `update_file`, this specific failure mode should be gone. If a dump still fails, it will be for some other real reason (command failure, bad config, etc.), but **this “all PASSED then FAILED at the end” behavior was due to the emoji/`update_file` issue.**

---

### 2) Does dumping save multiple files with incrementing numbers?

Yes, the dump path is designed to support multiple versions via the **config serial** logic:

In `Fw_get()`:

```python
# Resolve config serial: normal -> base; repaired -> next version
config_serial = get_config_serial_for_dump(base, repaired)
print(f"Config serial for dump: {config_serial}")
```

- For **normal boards** (`repaired=False`), `config_serial` is just the **base** serial (e.g. `111`), so you get files like:
  - `D:\rapture_dump_image\SonicLamb_111_fw.XUV`
  - `D:\rapture_dump_image\111_config.htf`

- For **repaired boards** (`repaired=True`), `get_config_serial_for_dump` is described in the docstring as:

  > first time creates `{base}_repaired_config.htf`; retries create `{base}_repaired_1_config.htf`, etc.

So conceptually you get:

- First repaired dump: `111_repaired_config.htf` and corresponding dump file
- Next repaired dump: `111_repaired_1_config.htf`
- Next: `111_repaired_2_config.htf`, and so on

The exact filenames depend on how `get_config_serial_for_dump` is implemented, but **yes**, the logic is built to create *different* config/dump filenames for each repaired attempt by incrementing the suffix on the `config_serial`.

## Fix: Serial cleared in lanes 2, 3, 4

**Cause:** On blur (including when Enter is pressed), the script read `row.pcb_serial_no` from the model. For lanes 2–4, the model often wasn’t updated yet when blur fired, so `row.pcb_serial_no` was empty and the serial was treated as cleared.

**Change:** Use the value from the DOM input first, then fall back to the model:

```javascript
const dom_val = ($inp.val() || "").toString().trim();
const model_val = (row.pcb_serial_no || "").toString().trim();
const new_serial = dom_val || model_val;
```

This uses the value the user typed in the input, even if the model hasn’t synced yet.

        return;

          lane_action_status: "",
          lane_action_message: "",
          lane_progress: 0,

That log is NOT a dump/flash test log. It’s your connector “standby / housekeeping” loop running every poll cycle.

What each line means (in plain English)

[PC_NAME] DESKTOP-2FK1FH7
Connector is alive and identifies which PC it is.

[JOBS] 1 ['PTS1_testing_form']
ERP has 1 PTS1 Test doc assigned to this PC (target_pc matches).

[PROCESS_DOC] PTS1_testing_form
Connector opened that doc to check lanes.

[FIND_COM CHECK] ... status=''
“Find COM Ports” is not requested right now, so connector does nothing for COM scan.

[LANE UPDATE VERIFY FAILED] ... field_write_failed: run_id,repaired_pcb ...
Connector is trying to flush “pending finalize updates” (your PENDING_FINALIZE retry queue).
But ERP refuses to write these fields because the child table does not have columns like:

run_id

repaired_pcb
(same problem also happens for last_heartbeat_at earlier)

### AI  ``

### 1) Is that the sole reason?

For the log you pasted (dump where all steps say PASSED but final status is FAILED):

**Yes, effectively this is the reason:**

- Hardware + commands all passed.
- Then `Fw_get()` calls `update_file(config_serial)`.
- Inside `update_file`, the emoji `✅` (and possibly `❌`) caused a **Unicode / charmap error** on Windows.
- That made `update_file` return `"FAILED"` (or raise), and your code does:

  ```python
  if update_ret == "PASSED":
      print("#####---- MAC extracted from dump HTF file ----####")
  else:
      print("#####---- MAC extraction/update FAILED ----####")
      test_return = "FAILED"
      test_log.append("MAC extraction/update FAILED")
  ```

- So **only because** `update_file` failed, `test_return` becomes `"FAILED"` and you see `Dump completed with status: FAILED`.

Now that we removed the emojis from `update_file`, this specific failure mode should be gone. If a dump still fails, it will be for some other real reason (command failure, bad config, etc.), but **this “all PASSED then FAILED at the end” behavior was due to the emoji/`update_file` issue.**

---

### 2) Does dumping save multiple files with incrementing numbers?

Yes, the dump path is designed to support multiple versions via the **config serial** logic:

In `Fw_get()`:

```python
# Resolve config serial: normal -> base; repaired -> next version
config_serial = get_config_serial_for_dump(base, repaired)
print(f"Config serial for dump: {config_serial}")
```

- For **normal boards** (`repaired=False`), `config_serial` is just the **base** serial (e.g. `111`), so you get files like:
  - `D:\rapture_dump_image\SonicLamb_111_fw.XUV`
  - `D:\rapture_dump_image\111_config.htf`

- For **repaired boards** (`repaired=True`), `get_config_serial_for_dump` is described in the docstring as:

  > first time creates `{base}_repaired_config.htf`; retries create `{base}_repaired_1_config.htf`, etc.

So conceptually you get:

- First repaired dump: `111_repaired_config.htf` and corresponding dump file
- Next repaired dump: `111_repaired_1_config.htf`
- Next: `111_repaired_2_config.htf`, and so on

The exact filenames depend on how `get_config_serial_for_dump` is implemented, but **yes**, the logic is built to create *different* config/dump filenames for each repaired attempt by incrementing the suffix on the `config_serial`.

### AI  ``

ERP and “the internet” are not the same path: **ERP** talks to your LAN server; **Google Sheets** needs **DNS + HTTPS to `oauth2.googleapis.com`**. ERP can be fine while **public Google hostnames** still fail.

## What’s going wrong

`getaddrinfo failed` for **`oauth2.googleapis.com`** means **this PC is not resolving that name** (or something is intercepting DNS). That happens **at import/startup** when `gspread` / Google auth tries to get a token — before dump/flash logic runs.

## Way forward (fix the PC / network)

Run these **on the same machine** that runs `ERP_PTS-1_COPY.py`:

1. **Check DNS for Google’s OAuth host**
   ```powershell
   nslookup oauth2.googleapis.com
   ```
   If this fails, the problem is DNS (not Python).

2. **Flush DNS cache (Windows)**
   ```powershell
   ipconfig /flushdns
   ```
   Then try `nslookup` again.

3. **Try another resolver temporarily**  
   In **Network adapter → IPv4 → DNS**, set e.g. **8.8.8.8** and **1.1.1.1**, or your router’s DNS if it forwards correctly. Corporate networks sometimes break only `*.googleapis.com` unless IT allows it.

4. **Check `hosts` and security software**
   - Open `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts` — ensure nothing blocks Google.
   - Temporarily rule out endpoint tools blocking Google APIs.

5. **Browser test**  
   Open: `https://oauth2.googleapis.com` — you should get a small JSON/error page, not “can’t resolve server”.

6. **Python-level check** (same interpreter as the script):
   ```powershell
   python -c "import socket; print(socket.getaddrinfo('oauth2.googleapis.com', 443))"
   ```
   If this throws, it confirms **system DNS** from Python’s view.

“Internet works” often means **browser works** (different DNS, DoH, or cache) while **system DNS** used by Python still fails — the steps above isolate that.

## If you must run without Google (bench / isolated LAN)

Then the **way forward** is a **product decision**: change the worker so **Sheets is optional** (e.g. env var `PTS1_DISABLE_GSHEET=1`) and skip `gspread` when unset/offline, with MAC still printed from HTF where possible. That’s a **code change** in `ERP_PTS-1_COPY.py` / `ERP_PTS-1.py`; say if you want that pattern applied in your repo’s `ERP_PTS-1.py` and I can outline or implement it.

**Bottom line:** Fix **DNS resolution to `oauth2.googleapis.com`** on that PC (or allow it through firewall/policy). ERP working does not prove that path works.

**No — and it isn’t meant to be “fixed” away.**

In your workspace copy `ERP_PTS-1.py`, `worker_mode` still ends the same way:

```641:646:c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\pts1 test\ERP_PTS-1.py
    # IMPORTANT: return proper exit code for connector
    # PASSED -> 0, FAILED -> 1
    if str(ret).strip().upper() == "PASSED":
        sys.exit(0)
    else:
        sys.exit(1)
```

**`SystemExit: 1`** here is **on purpose**: the debugger treats `sys.exit(1)` as an exception, but the script is signaling **“operation failed”** to whatever launched it (e.g. the connector). If dump/flash returns anything other than **`PASSED`**, you will still get exit code **1**.

So:

- **Same logic** as your `ERP_PTS-1_COPY.py` traceback (line numbers may differ slightly).
- **“Fix”** = fix why **`Fw_get` / `Fw_flash`** end with **`FAILED`** (logs in `PTS_Logs\slot{N}_{dump|flash}.log`, COM/ISP/hardware), not removing `sys.exit(1)`.

If you want the debugger to stop breaking on that, configure “don’t break on `SystemExit`” or run without catching exit, or refactor to `return 0/1` from `worker_mode` and `raise SystemExit` only in `if __name__` — behavior for the parent process should stay **0 = success, 1 = failure**.

### 2. **Lane 1–4 ↔ USB slots (no left/right packing for USB scan)**
**`com_scan_headless.py`**
- Builds **`slots`**: a list of **4** strings — COM for that USB “slot”, or `""` if nothing there.
- Uses the **rightmost `USB(n)` with n in 1..4** in the device location path (same idea as a 4-port hub).
- Example: only physical **port 2** → often `["", "106", "", ""]` → **only lane 2** gets `106`.
- Still returns **`ports`** (non-empty COMs only) for older logic.
- **Pyserial** is used **only if** USB/PnP fails, and it **does not** emit `slots` (no topology), so the connector falls back.

**`PTS1 Station Connector.py`**
- **`COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "slot"`** (default): if JSON has **`slots`**, lanes are updated from `slots[0..3]`.
- **`COM_PORT_FALLBACK_MODE = "left"`**: if there is **no** `slots` (pyserial/CIM-only), COMs are filled with **left** packing (change to `"right"` if you prefer).
- **`run_com_scan()`** returns **`(ports, slots)`**; background scan compares a signature that includes `slots`.
- **Find COM** sends **`slots`** in the API body when present.

**Server script `update_find_com_result`**
- If **`slots`** is a list of **≥ 4** entries, it writes **`com_port`** for the first four lane rows from **`slots[0..3]`** (empty string clears COM).
- Otherwise it keeps the old **`ports`** list behavior.

---

- Slot detection assumes the **leaf hub index** in the PnP path is **1–4**. Odd hubs (only `USB(6)`, etc.) may not map; then **`slots` may be omitted** and **fallback** left/right is used.
- Deploy: **`com_scan_headless.py`**, **`PTS1 Station Connector.py`**, and the **server script** copy on the ERP server.

Here’s my current understanding of the versions in the new folder:

- **`PTS1 Station Connector.py`**:  
  - Polls `PTS1 Test` docs for `target_pc == this hostname`.  
  - Runs `com_scan_headless.py` every `COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC`, gets up to 4 COM “numbers”, and **updates per lane** COM via `lane_update()` → `api_cmd="update_lane_fields"` (never overwrites the whole child table).  
  - For each doc, finds lanes 1..4 where `lane_action_status == "Requested"`, and runs them in parallel with `ThreadPoolExecutor`, with an `IN_FLIGHT` set so a lane isn’t started twice.  
  - For each lane:
    - Validates `lane_action` (`VERIFY/DUMP/FLASH`) → maps to `dump`/`flash`.  
    - If missing serial or COM, marks lane Failed + Done via `lane_update`.  
    - Claims lane via `lane_update` (sets `lane_status="Running"`, `lane_action_status="Running"`, progress 1, clears `lane_log`).  
    - Spawns `ERP_PTS-1.py` with `--slot`, `--operation`, `--serial`, `--comport`.  
    - Streams stdout line by line, appends to a local `log_cache`, and **every few seconds** fetches latest lane from ERP and pushes merged `lane_log` + `lane_progress` via `lane_update()`.  
    - Uses regex to detect `Extracted Bluetooth MAC Address: XX:XX:...` and immediately calls `patch_lane_mac()`, which reads the doc, checks if `mac_id` is already same; if not, uses `lane_update(docname, lane_no, {"mac_id": mac})`.  
    - On process end, falls back to parse MAC from remaining `log_cache` if not seen live.  
    - Computes `final_lane_status` (`Completed`/`Failed`) based on `rc`, builds a message, and then calls `call_pts1_api` **once** with `api_cmd="record_lane_run"` sending docname, lane_no, serial, op, rc, message and mac.  
    - Fetches doc again, merges any existing `lane_log` with leftover `log_cache`, then does a final `lane_update` with `lane_status`, `lane_action_status="Done"`, message, progress=100, final log.  
    - On any exception, marks lane Failed + Done via `lane_update`.  
  - Parent `PTS1 Test.test_status` is set to Running when any lane is running, and to Completed/Failed once all lanes are idle and at least one has failed.  

- **`pts api server script 02-03-2026 - Copy.py` (server `pts1_api`)**:  
  - Extracts `payload` from `frappe.form_dict` (handles both `args` dict/string and direct keys) and routes on `api_cmd` (lowercased).  
  - Supports:
    - `request_lane_action`: validates docname, lane_no, `VERIFY/FLASH`, ensures lane has `pcb_serial_no` and `com_port`, then sets `lane_action`, `lane_action_status="Requested"`, `lane_status="Queued"`, progress 0, clears message + error, and optionally sets parent `test_status="Queued"`.  
    - `reset_lane`: clears all test-related fields on that lane (status, logs, errors, result json, mac, fw_file, etc.) and resets to Pending.  
    - `request_find_com`: marks parent fields `find_com_status="Requested"`, `find_com_message=""`.  
    - `update_find_com_result`: updates `find_com_status` and `find_com_message`, and if Done, assigns `com_port` to lanes 1..4 in order from a `ports` list.  
    - `update_lane_fields`: the **only atomic lane update** API. Reads the doc, finds the lane, and only allows a whitelisted set of fields (lane_action, lane_action_status, lane_status, lane_progress, lane_log, error_message, mac_id, lane_result_json, pcb_serial_no, com_port, etc.).  
    - `record_lane_run`: called by connector once per dump/flash. Robust UPSERT into `PTS1 Lane Result` keyed by serial using `frappe.db.exists`:
      - Sets `pcb_serial_no`, `lane_no`, updates `dump_count`/`flash_count`, statuses, `*_first_at`/`*_last_at`, stores `mac_id` if provided, and appends a bounded history line into `lane_result_json`.  
    - `upload_result_to_master_ledger`: implements the full upload logic:
      - Requires lane Done; decides `pts1_status` = Pass if lane_status Completed, else Fail.  
      - Looks up `PCB Ledger` primarily by `pcb_serial_no`, with docname fallbacks.  
      - Verifies the ledger is in PTS testing via lifecycle/status/timeline.  
      - Looks up `PCB Master` by `pcb_serial_no` (with docname fallback); updates `pts1_status`, `pts1_date` (IST), last_event_ref fields, and `mac_id` if available.  
      - Computes `overall_status` from pts1/2/3 and writes it to Master and Ledger; also updates Ledger’s `pts1_status`, `pts1_date`, `overall_status`, `last_tested_on`, and last_event_ref + `mac_id`.  
      - UPSERTs `PTS1 Lane Result` again with full lane snapshot: com, mac, fw_file, lane action/status/message, lane_status/step/progress, lane_log, error_message, with bounded history.  
      - Marks the lane’s `lane_result_json` with an “uploaded=1;uploaded_at=...;pts1_result_id=...;uploaded_run_id=...” marker, and saves the PTS doc.  
      - Idempotent: detects the marker and same run id but deliberately does not throw, allowing re‑upload.  
      - MAC source: prefers `lane.mac_id`, but if empty, falls back to the `PTS1 Lane Result` record for that serial.  

- **`pts1 client script.js`** (current in this folder):  
  - On load/refresh ensures exactly 4 lanes exist with default Pending state.  
  - Hooks a model event on child rows: when `pcb_serial_no` changes to a new non‑empty value, it **resets all test state** (status, action, progress, logs, result json, mac, fw_file) but keeps `com_port` and lane number; then does a debounced autosave.  
  - Helper functions to check busy/done/completed, find a lane row, and see whether any lanes are active.  
  - COM scan:
    - Button `find_com_port` calls `request_find_com` which hits `pts1_api` with `api_cmd="request_find_com"`.  
    - Auto request COM scan when some lane has a serial but missing COM and `find_com_status` is idle.  
    - Shows a “COM Assigned: ...” toast once `find_com_status == Done` and lanes have COMs.  
  - Actions:
    - Dump/Flash buttons call `request_action`, which **calls `pts1_api`** with `api_cmd="request_lane_action"` for that lane; no direct bulk overwrites.  
    - Upload button calls `pts1_api` with `api_cmd="upload_result_to_master_ledger"` (docname + lane_no).  
    - Per-lane Reset calls `pts1_api` with `api_cmd="reset_lane"` (docname + lane_no) instead of manually clearing fields.  
    - “Reset All (keep COM)” button clears serials and lane state in all 4 lanes (but leaves `com_port`), then saves + reloads.  
  - Renders a dashboard with one row per lane: colored progress bar and 4 buttons (Dump / Flash / Upload / Reset), with correct enable/disable rules, and auto‑refreshes the form every ~900 ms while any lane is Requested/Running.  
  - Syncs each lane’s log into separate read‑only fields `lane1_log_view` … `lane4_log_view` if present on the doctype.  

- **`com_scan_headless.py`** (fast version):  
  - Runs a trimmed PowerShell query (`Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly`) filtered only to USB devices whose `FriendlyName` ends with “- 0112”‑style patterns, with progress output disabled, and returns JSON with up to 4 COM “numbers” (e.g. `"111"`, `"112"`).  
  - Groups USB devices by hub socket key, prefers non‑generic friendly names, extracts `VID:PID` and parses the trailing numeric code from the name as your lane COM.  
  - Retries a few times, then prints `{"ok": true, "ports": [...], "depth": N}` to stdout or `{"ok": false, ...}` on failure.  
  - This is what the connector calls in `run_com_scan()` to auto‑assign com ports per lane.

Everything in this new folder is consistent with the goal and the rules we defined earlier: **no bulk child-table overwrites from the connector, record_lane_run once per run, proper MAC capture and propagation, and idempotent uploads.**

### AI  ``

Here’s how it behaves with the code you have now.

### `COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "right"` (current default)

The scan only gives a **flat list** of COM numbers (e.g. `['106','114','107']`). There is **no** notion of “which physical lane is empty” inside that list.

With **3** numbers and **right** alignment we do:

| Lane | COM   |
|------|--------|
| 1    | empty  |
| 2    | 106    |
| 3    | 114    |
| 4    | 107    |

So you get **`nil, 106, 114, 107`**-style behavior: **leading** lanes stay empty, values are packed **toward lane 4**.

### Why not `112, nil, 114, 107`?

That pattern means “something in slot 2 is missing but slot 1 still has 112.” The scanner would have to return **four slots** (with an explicit empty in the middle). Today **`com_scan_headless`** only returns **connected** COMs, so a list like `['112','114','107']` is **three** devices — with **right** mode that becomes **`nil, 112, 114, 107`**, not `112, nil, 114, 107`.

So:

- **Yes**: missing COMs show as **empty** on the ERP lane.
- **Leading** empties when there are fewer than 4 ports → use **`right`** (what you want for “port 1 empty”).
- **A hole in the middle** (`112, nil, 114, 107`) would need the scan (or another mapping) to output **placeholders per fixed slot**; the connector alone cannot infer that from `['112','114','107']`.

### `COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "left"`

With the same three ports you get **`106, 114, 107, nil`** (fill from lane 1, **clear** any extra lane at the end). Still no automatic middle `nil`.

### AI  ``

### Solid, non‑manual solution

To make this robust and avoid manual field edits, the behavior should be:

1. **Reset button becomes a true “Stop + Clear” for dead runs**
   - When you press **Reset** on a lane that is `Requested` / `Running` / `AbortRequested`:
     - ERP **still asks** the connector to abort.
     - **But** after that, the server immediately clears that lane’s state in DB:
       - `lane_action_status = ""`
       - `lane_status = "Pending"`
       - `abort_requested = 0`
       - `run_id = ""`
       - live fields + logs cleared.
   - That way, even if the connector is dead, the ERP side lane is guaranteed to end in a **clean idle** state after Reset, and Upload checks will no longer be blocked by `AbortRequested`.

2. **Upload guard stays simple**
   - Upload only allowed when:
     - `lane_action_status == "Done"` (normal case), OR
     - `lane_action_status == ""` but `lane_status == "Completed"` (if you reset after a clean Done).
   - Upload **always blocked** when state is any of: `Requested`, `Running`, `AbortRequested`.

3. **Result:**
   - If a lane ever misbehaves, operator just hits **Reset** once.
   - After Reset finishes (1–2 seconds), lane is guaranteed to be fully cleared; Upload for other lanes is unaffected, and that lane can be re‑Flashed from scratch.
   - No need to open child rows or touch fields manually.

If you confirm, I’ll wire this exact behavior into `reset_lane` on the server + adjust the client to trust it, so you get this “hard reset” guarantee.

### Current behavior (with the code we have now)

- **If you CLEAR the serial (make it blank) in a lane row**:
  - That row is **fully reset**:
    - `pcb_serial_no` becomes empty
    - `com_port` becomes empty
    - `mac_id`, `lane_status`, `lane_action(_status/message)`, `lane_progress`, `lane_step`, `error_message`, `lane_log`, `lane_result_json`, `fw_file` are all cleared / reset.
  - Visually: only `Lane No` (and the row index) remain; all other columns go blank/default.

- **If you CHANGE the serial from one non‑empty value to another non‑empty value**:
  - The row is **logically reset for a new PCB**, but **COM port is kept**:
    - New `pcb_serial_no` is set.
    - `lane_status`, `lane_action(_status/message)`, `lane_progress`, `lane_step`, `error_message`, `lane_log`, `mac_id`, `lane_result_json`, `fw_file` are cleared / reset.
    - `com_port` is preserved so you don’t have to re‑scan COMs.
  - Then when you press Dump/Flash for that lane, **all new info for that PCB** (log, MAC, status, etc.) will be filled for that same row.

So:

- **“Resetting lane = row becomes empty”** is true when you clear the serial (blank).  
- When you enter a **new serial**, the row is reset except for COM (by design); all new test info will belong to that serial once you run Dump/Flash.

If you instead want the row to truly be empty (including COM) every time the serial changes (even non‑blank), I can switch it so COM is also cleared on any serial change.

```js
frappe.model.on(child_dt, {
  pcb_serial_no(doc, cdt, cdn) {
    // ... guards ...

    const new_serial = String(doc.pcb_serial_no || "").trim();
    const key = cdn;
    const old_serial = String(window.__pts1_prev_serial_map[key] || "").trim();

    if (new_serial === old_serial) return;      // no change

    window.__pts1_prev_serial_map[key] = new_serial;

    const reset_fields = {
      lane_status: "Pending",
      lane_action: "",
      lane_action_status: "",
      lane_action_message: "",
      lane_progress: 0,
      lane_step: "",
      error_message: "",
      lane_log: "",
      mac_id: "",
      lane_result_json: "",
      fw_file: ""
    };

    if (!new_serial) {                  // serial cleared
      reset_fields.com_port = "";
      reset_fields.pcb_serial_no = "";
    }

    Object.keys(reset_fields).forEach((k) => {
      frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, k, reset_fields[k]);
    });

    frm.refresh_field("lanes");
    // debounced autosave...
  }
});
```

# ❌ What is STILL WRONG / risky (must fix)

## 1) **Your “auto-reset on serial change” logic is still too aggressive**

Right now, whenever a serial changes, you do:

```js
clear_lane_row(... KEEP_COM_ON_NEW_SERIAL);
frappe.model.set_value(... "pcb_serial_no", new_serial);
```

That means:

* You type serial in lane2
* blur happens
* script clears lane fields (including *possibly serial momentarily*)
* grid refresh happens
* sometimes Frappe grid sees “serial empty” during refresh and **clears the input**

That is exactly the symptom you had earlier:
**lane2/3/4 serial gets cleared when pressing Enter / clicking away**.

### ✅ Fix rule (correct order)

When serial changes, do this order:

1. **Set serial first**
2. Then clear other fields **without touching pcb_serial_no**
3. Never do `frm.refresh_field("lanes")` immediately in the same tick

So you need a “clear without serial” function.

---

## 2) You have **TWO competing save paths**

* `save_lane_via_api()` inside blur handler
* `lane_patch_to_db()` inside Dump/Flash click

This causes race conditions:

* blur triggers api update
* immediately you click Dump, it patches again
* then background refresh comes
* doc version mismatch happens (“modified after you loaded it”)

### ✅ Fix rule

* For normal typing: **don’t patch to server every blur**
* Only patch on:

  * Dump/Flash click
  * Find COM completion (server/connector updates)
  * Reset
  * Manual Save button

Meaning: **remove `save_lane_via_api()` from blur** OR gate it with “only when user has completed row”.

* When you click Dump2, it should **push lane2 to DB first**, then request action

So the correct architecture is:

### ✅ UI editing is local only (no API writes on blur)

* capture serial into model
* do NOT reload_doc
* do NOT call update_lane_fields on blur

### ✅ On Dump/Flash click

* commit_active_grid_cell()
* lane_patch_to_db(lane_no)  ✅ (you already have)
* then request_lane_action ✅

That’s airtight.

Now the behavior is:

- **Change serial to a new non‑empty value** in a lane:
  - Lane is reset (status/action/progress/log/mac/result/fw) but **COM port is kept**; serial stays as you typed.

- **Clear the serial (empty string) in a lane**:
  - Lane is fully reset: all test fields **plus** `pcb_serial_no` and `com_port` are cleared, and `mac_id` is also cleared.
  - Grid is refreshed immediately so the MAC ID column is wiped for that row.

Try again by clearing the serial in that second row; the MAC ID and other lane fields should now disappear for that lane.

### Short answer

Those two structural issues are already fixed in the version you just pasted. You’re now in the “production‑stable” shape you described.

### How your current code matches the rules

- **No server writes on blur anymore**
  - `save_lane_via_api` and `debounced_autosave` are gone from `setup_auto_reset_on_serial_change`.
  - Blur handler only:
    - Reads `new_serial` (captured / DOM / model).
    - Updates the model.
    - Clears lane fields **locally**.
    - Does a small delayed `refresh_field("lanes")`.

- **Serial change: set serial first, then clear (without touching serial)**
  - On serial cleared:
    - `frappe.model.set_value(..., "pcb_serial_no", "")`
    - `clear_lane_row(..., KEEP_COM_ON_CLEAR)` (this is OK because we explicitly set serial to empty).
  - On serial changed:

function setup_auto_reset_on_serial_change(frm) {
  if (frm.__pts1_serial_reset_hooked) return;
  frm.__pts1_serial_reset_hooked = true;

  const lanes_field = frm.fields_dict.lanes;

  if (!window.__pts1_prev_serial_map) window.__pts1_prev_serial_map = {};

  frappe.model.on(child_dt, {

      if (!frm?.doc) return;
      if (doc.parenttype !== "PTS1 Test") return;
      if (doc.parent !== frm.doc.name) return;

      const new_serial = ((doc.pcb_serial_no || "") + "").trim();
      const key = cdn;
      const old_serial = ((window.__pts1_prev_serial_map[key] || "") + "").trim();

      // Always track latest
      window.__pts1_prev_serial_map[key] = new_serial;

      // If user CLEARS serial => clear the whole lane row (INCLUDING COM + MAC + status)
      if (!new_serial) {

          lane_action: "",

          lane_action_message: "",
          lane_progress: 0,
          lane_step: "",

          lane_log: "",
          mac_id: "",
          lane_result_json: "",
          fw_file: "",
          com_port: ""        // ✅ clear COM too (row becomes empty)

        if (frm.__pts1_autosave_timer) clearTimeout(frm.__pts1_autosave_timer);
        frm.__pts1_autosave_timer = setTimeout(() => {
          frm.__pts1_autosave_timer = null;
          if (!frm.is_new() && frm.is_dirty()) frm.save().catch(() => {});
        }, 400);

        return;
      }

      // If first time typing (no old_serial) => just reset lane state (keep COM as-is)
      // If serial changed => reset lane state
      if (new_serial !== old_serial) {
        const reset_fields = {
          lane_status: "Pending",
          lane_action: "",
          lane_action_status: "",
          lane_action_message: "",
          lane_progress: 0,
          lane_step: "",

          lane_log: "",

        if (frm.__pts1_autosave_timer) clearTimeout(frm.__pts1_autosave_timer);
        frm.__pts1_autosave_timer = setTimeout(() => {
          frm.__pts1_autosave_timer = null;
          if (!frm.is_new() && frm.is_dirty()) frm.save().catch(() => {});
        }, 400);
      }
    }
  });
}

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Root cause
`request_find_com` called `frappe.db.set_value("PTS1 Test", …, "find_com_status", …)`. Those columns **do not exist** on `tabPTS1 Test` until Custom Fields exist **and** you run **`bench migrate`**. MySQL then raises **1054 Unknown column**, and the script turned that into a `ValidationError`.

### Fix (two layers)

**1. Server script (`pts api server script 02-03-2026 - Copy.py`)**  
- **`db_set_find_com_parent`**: Still tries the real columns first. On **1054 / Unknown column**, it no longer throws; it writes the same state into **`tabDefaultValue`** with keys like `pts1_find_com_<DOCNAME>_st` / `_msg` (`parent='__default'`).  
- **`read_find_com_merged`**: Reads from the document when present, otherwise from that fallback.  
- **`get_status_snapshot`**: Uses **`read_find_com_merged`**, so the browser poll gets **Requested / Running / Done / Failed** even without Custom Fields.  
- **`peek_find_com_state`**: New `api_cmd` so the connector can see Find COM state when the REST document JSON doesn’t include those fields.

**2. Connector (`PTS1 Station Connector.py`, version **2026-03-25_v3`)**  
- If `get_doc` has no `find_com_status`, it calls **`peek_find_com_state`** so **`process_find_com_request`** still sees **Requested** and runs the scan.

**3. Client (`pts1 client script.js`)**  
- After a successful Find COM request, if the form doesn’t have **`find_com_status`**, it still sets **`frm.doc.find_com_status = "Requested"`** so polling/UI behave until the first snapshot returns.

**4. Optional proper DB columns**  
- **`ADD_FIND_COM_CUSTOM_FIELDS.py`**: One-shot `create_custom_fields` + then **`bench migrate`** so you get real fields on the form and can drop reliance on the DefaultValue fallback later.

### What you need to do
1. **Paste the updated Server Script** into ERPNext **Server Script** `pts1_api` and save.  
2. **Deploy** connector **v3** on the station PC.  
3. **Clear cache** on the site (`bench clear-cache`) if the script is cached.  
4. **Try Find COM again** — it should queue and complete without the “database setup missing” error.  
5. When convenient, run **`ADD_FIND_COM_CUSTOM_FIELDS.py`** via **bench console** + **`bench migrate`** so **`find_com_*`** live on **`tabPTS1 Test`** (cleaner long-term; fallback rows are cleared when the real columns are used).

You’re **very close**. Your current stack (run_id + strict writes + append_lane_log + stale marking) will stop 95% of “ERP missed feedback”.

But there are **5 hard bugs / edge-cases** still in what you pasted that can *still* cause “ERP didn’t update / stuck running / missed last result”.

I’ll point them out and give **exact patches**.

---

## 1) 🚨 BUG: `claim_lane` currently overwrites server run_id with connector fallback

Right now server does:

```py
if run_id:
    frappe.db.set_value(..., "run_id", run_id)
```

But UI already generated a run_id at `request_lane_action`.
If connector passes fallback `doc|lane` (or empty) then server will **replace** the real run_id and your guard becomes meaningless.

### ✅ Fix (server `claim_lane`)

Only set run_id **if empty** on DB.

Replace this:

```py
if run_id:
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id", run_id, update_modified=False)
```

with:

```py
cur_run_id = (frappe.db.get_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id") or "").strip()
if not cur_run_id and run_id:
    frappe.db.set_value(child_dt, rn, "run_id", run_id, update_modified=False)
```

Also: if `cur_run_id` exists, return it in response so connector can use it.

```py
out = {"ok": True, "api_cmd": api_cmd, "docname": docname, "lane_no": lane_no, "run_id": (cur_run_id or run_id)}
```

---

## 2) 🚨 BUG: `append_lane_log` can erase logs because you `.strip()` merged

In server you do:

```py
merged = (existing + chunk).strip()
```

That removes leading/trailing newlines and can unintentionally change log content. Worse: if `existing` is huge and chunk is small, strip is fine, but it’s unnecessary and sometimes “eats” separators.

### ✅ Fix

Use:

```py
merged = (existing + chunk)
```

and then truncate:

```py
if len(merged) > 15000:
    merged = merged[-15000:]
```

No `.strip()`.

---

## 3) 🚨 BUG: you still sometimes write full `lane_log` from connector finalize

After you append logs server-side, your finalize payload still includes:

```py
final_fields["lane_log"] = final_log
```

That can **overwrite** server log if a late append arrives, or if finalize fetch gets stale data.

### ✅ Fix (connector)

Stop sending `lane_log` in finalize/abort updates when using append_lane_log.

In connector, in both finalize and abort_fields: **remove** `"lane_log": ...`.

So:

```py
abort_fields.update({
  "lane_status": "Aborted",
  "lane_action_status": "Done",
  ...
  # REMOVE lane_log
})
```

and:

```py
final_fields.update({
  "lane_status": final_lane_status,
  "lane_action_status": "Done",
  ...
  # REMOVE lane_log
})
```

Logs should be ONLY via append_lane_log.

---

## 4) ⚠️ Stale marking inside `get_status_snapshot` is risky

You are mutating DB inside a “read-only poll” endpoint. It will work, but it can cause:

* unnecessary commits every poll
* accidental staling during brief network hiccups
* extra DB write load

### ✅ Better approach (still simple)

Make stale marking a separate api_cmd: `mark_stale_lanes` (or do it in connector loop once per doc). But if you keep it in snapshot:

**Add a guard** so it only writes once:

Only set stale if current status is Running AND lane_status != Stale already.

```py
cur_ls = (r.get("lane_status") or "").strip().lower()
if cur_ls == "stale":
    continue
```

And increase threshold to **90–120 seconds** (60 is too aggressive for real-world lag).

---

## 5) ⚠️ Parent finalize doesn’t consider `stale`

Your `finalize_parent_if_idle()` checks active statuses:

```py
("requested","running","abortrequested")
```

If a lane becomes Stale, parent may incorrectly become Completed/Failed even though UI shows Stale.

### ✅ Fix

Include stale as active (so parent remains “Running/Queued” until user resets):

```py
active = any(safe_str(x.get("lane_action_status")).lower() in ("requested","running","abortrequested","stale") for x in lanes)
```

Also count stale as failed if you want parent “Failed”:

* Either treat stale as failed
* Or keep parent “Running” until reset (recommended)

4. **Heartbeat timestamp set server-side**
5. **Any DB write failure is returned to connector**

   * connector retries & prints failed fields
6. **Stale detection doesn’t auto-complete parent**

### USER  ``

To make sure ERP **never “misses” feedback** from the connector, you need 3 layers of protection:

1. **Delivery reliability** (retries + verification)
2. **Idempotency** (same update can be safely re-sent)
3. **Stale-job recovery** (if connector dies mid-run, ERP can auto-release / user can abort)

Below is the exact practical approach that works at scale.

---

## 1) Make every connector → ERP update “retry + verify”

Right now `lane_update()` does:

* 1 HTTP call
* assumes success if no exception

That is why you get “connector finished but ERP still shows Requested/Running”.

### Change `lane_update()` to: retry + read-back verify

Use a tiny helper:

```python
def lane_update_verified(docname: str, lane_no: int, fields: dict, expect_key=None, expect_val=None):
    # expect_key/val optional: verify server actually stored it
    last_err = None
    for i in range(PATCH_RETRIES):
        try:
            lane_update(docname, lane_no, fields)  # your existing call_pts1_api wrapper
            if expect_key:
                d = get_doc(DOCTYPE_PARENT, docname)
                r = find_lane_row(d, lane_no) if d else None
                if r and safe_str(r.get(expect_key)).strip().lower() == safe_str(expect_val).strip().lower():
                    return True
                last_err = "verify failed " + str(expect_key)
            else:
                return True
        except Exception as e:
            last_err = repr(e)
        time.sleep(PATCH_RETRY_SLEEP * (i + 1))
    print("[LANE UPDATE VERIFY FAILED]", docname, lane_no, last_err, fields)
    return False
```

Then:

* **Claim** must be `lane_update_verified(... expect lane_action_status == "Running")`
* **Finalize** must be `lane_update_verified(... expect lane_action_status == "Done")`

If claim verify fails → **do not start subprocess**. This prevents re-runs + stuck statuses.

---

## 2) Add `run_id` + make updates idempotent

ERP misses updates mostly because “old run” and “new run” collide.

### Add fields in lane child table (PTS1 Test → lanes):

* `run_id` (Data)
* `run_seq` (Int) optional
* `last_heartbeat_at` (Datetime)
* `connector_name` (Data)

### When queueing from UI (server `request_lane_action`)

Generate a run id and store it:

* `run_id = docname + "|" + lane_no + "|" + frappe.generate_hash(length=8)`
  (If `generate_hash` blocked in RestrictedPython, do a timestamp string like `now_dt` + lane_no.)

Then all connector updates MUST include `run_id` and server must **ignore updates that don’t match current run_id**.

**Why this matters:** even if connector sends late “Done” from an older run, ERP won’t accept it.

### Server-side guard inside `update_lane_fields`

Before applying `fields`, do:

* read current `run_id` of lane
* if incoming `fields.run_id` exists and doesn’t match → reject/ignore

This single thing eliminates “ERP shows Requested again” type corruption.

---

## 3) Use Compare-And-Set (CAS) for claiming a lane

Your current flow:

* connector sees Requested
* connector writes Running
* but another loop / retry can race

Fix: create a dedicated server command `claim_lane` that only succeeds if status is still Requested.

### New server api_cmd: `claim_lane`

Logic:

* if lane_action_status != "Requested": return ok=False
* else set lane_action_status="Running", lane_status="Running", set run_id if not present
* commit
* return ok=True

Connector must call `claim_lane` and proceed ONLY if ok=True.

This is the “atomic lock” that prevents duplicates.

---

## 4) Heartbeat + stale detection (so ERP can recover)

Even with retries, a Windows PC can crash mid-run. ERP needs a way to detect “Running but dead”.

### Connector: heartbeat every 5–10 seconds

While subprocess is alive:

* update `last_heartbeat_at = now`
* also push `lane_progress` and maybe last log line

### ERP: stale rule

If:

* lane_action_status == "Running"
* AND `now - last_heartbeat_at > 60s` (choose 60–120)
  → mark lane as **Stale/Disconnected** (UI shows “Connector offline”)
  → enable **Stop/Reset** immediately

This makes “ERP waiting forever” impossible.

---

## 5) Make finalize “eventually consistent” even if network dies

After subprocess exits, connector should keep trying finalize until it sees Done stored.

Simple pattern:

* write finalize
* verify read-back
* if fail, keep retrying for up to e.g. 2 minutes in a background loop OR next poll cycle tries again when it sees “Running but process already ended”.

### Store local “pending finalize” in connector memory

When process exits, store:

`PENDING_FINAL[(doc,lane)] = final_payload`

Each main loop iteration tries to flush pending finals first.

This guarantees ERP eventually gets the final state.

---

## 6) Stop overwriting lane fields from other sources

You already improved server-side to use `db.set_value` lane-only. Keep it.

But one more risk:

* UI `frm.reload_doc()` during run can overwrite local edits, but not DB.
* So the bigger risk is **any code calling `pts.save()` on parent while lanes running**.

Rule: **never call `doc.save()` on parent from connector**, except in a dedicated place where you only touch parent fields (not lanes). You’re already using lane_update which is good.

---

# Minimum changes that give you 90% reliability (do these first)

1. `lane_update_verified()` + claim verify gate (don’t run if claim not confirmed)
2. `claim_lane` CAS endpoint
3. `run_id` match guard (ignore stale updates)
4. heartbeat + stale detection

If you want, paste your connector `run_lane_job()` and I’ll rewrite it in one clean version with:

* CAS claim
* run_id
* heartbeat
* pending finalize queue
* verified updates only

That will stop ERP from “missing feedback” permanently.

Here’s the end-to-end flow after the latest changes (connector + headless scan).

### Components and roles
- **com_scan_headless.py**  
  - Returns two things:  
    - `slots`: four strings `[A,B,C,D]` mapped to USB topology (lane 1–4). Empty string = nothing in that slot.  
    - `ports`: non-empty COM list for backward compatibility.
- **PTS1 Station Connector.py** (running on the test PC)  
  - Polls ERP, runs background COM scans, updates ERP lanes, runs Dump/Flash, does preflight safety.
- **Server script `pts1_api`** (ERP)  
  - Receives Find COM results (including `slots`), updates lane `com_port` accordingly.

### Startup
- Prints config. Runs a **startup COM scan** (short timeout 25s).  
- Captures the first non-empty scan as **baseline** (`BASELINE_SLOTS/PORTS`).  
- Enters main loop.

### Continuous background COM sync
- Every **`COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC`** (2s):
  - Runs **com_scan_headless** with full timeout (90s).
  - Captures/updates **baseline** if it was empty.
  - Applies results to ERP lanes:
    - If `slots` exist → `lane1..4` get `slots[0..3]` (empty clears COM).
    - Else, falls back to `ports` packing (`COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE`, default `slot` with fallback `left`).
  - Only applies when the scan signature changes.

### Find COM button (ERP)
- Server script now accepts `slots`:
  - If `slots` (length ≥4) are present, writes `com_port` lane-by-lane from `slots[0..3]`.
  - Otherwise, uses the older `ports` list.
- Parent fields `find_com_status/find_com_message` are set (ensure those Custom Fields exist).

### Preflight before each Dump/Flash (per lane)
When a lane is Requested and we claim it:
1. Run **com_scan_headless** again (fresh, full timeout).
2. If that scan is empty and a **baseline** exists, use the baseline instead.
3. Compute the COM for **this lane**:
   - Prefer `slots[lane-1]` when available.
   - Otherwise, pack `ports` with fallback mode.
4. Compare vs ERP `com_port` and resolve:
   - **Both set & equal** → run with that COM.
   - **Both set but differ** → with `COM_PREFLIGHT_TRUST_SCAN=True` (default), write the scanned COM back to ERP (with `run_id`) and run. If False, fail with mismatch.
   - **Scan has COM, ERP empty** → write to ERP, run.
   - **Scan empty, ERP has COM** → by default **fail** (message tells you to fix USB/Find COM). If you set `COM_PREFLIGHT_ALLOW_ERP_IF_SCAN_EMPTY=True`, it will run using ERP (risky).
5. If preflight fails → lane is finalized Failed/Done with the reason; process stops before calling `ERP_PTS-1.py`.

### CLI execution
- After preflight resolves COM, it starts `ERP_PTS-1.py` with `--slot <lane> --comport <resolved COM> ...`.
- Logs stream to ERP via `append_lane_log` as before; MAC extraction, heartbeat, finalize unchanged.

### Session baseline
- First non-empty scan (startup or background) is stored as baseline.
- Used only if a later **preflight scan** returns no devices; lets you keep running with the last known good layout instead of hard failing because Windows briefly hid the device.

### Key settings (current defaults)
```python
COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "slot"      # prefer slots A-D
COM_PORT_FALLBACK_MODE = "left"    # used only if no slots from scan
COM_PREFLIGHT_BEFORE_RUN = True
COM_PREFLIGHT_TRUST_SCAN = True
COM_PREFLIGHT_ALLOW_ERP_IF_SCAN_EMPTY = False
COM_SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC = 2.0
COM_SCAN_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT = 90
COM_SCAN_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC = 25
```

### What you see in logs
- Startup: `[COMSCAN] startup test ...` then `[COMSCAN TEST] ports=... slots=...`
- Background: `[COM UPDATED] <doc> slots=[...] mode=slot`
- Preflight mismatch: `[COM PREFLIGHT] lane X clash ERP=... scan=... -> trust scan`
- Preflight fail (scan empty vs ERP): lane is marked Failed with the message.

This matches your requested behavior:
- Always keep ERP lanes in sync with live USB slot layout.
- Before running Dump/Flash on a lane, double-check that lane’s COM against a fresh (or baseline) scan and reconcile before launching the CLI.

### Current behavior (with the code we have now)

- **If you CLEAR the serial (make it blank) in a lane row**:
  - That row is **fully reset**:
    - `pcb_serial_no` becomes empty
    - `com_port` becomes empty
    - `mac_id`, `lane_status`, `lane_action(_status/message)`, `lane_progress`, `lane_step`, `error_message`, `lane_log`, `lane_result_json`, `fw_file` are all cleared / reset.
  - Visually: only `Lane No` (and the row index) remain; all other columns go blank/default.

- **If you CHANGE the serial from one non‑empty value to another non‑empty value**:
  - The row is **logically reset for a new PCB**, but **COM port is kept**:
    - New `pcb_serial_no` is set.
    - `lane_status`, `lane_action(_status/message)`, `lane_progress`, `lane_step`, `error_message`, `lane_log`, `mac_id`, `lane_result_json`, `fw_file` are cleared / reset.
    - `com_port` is preserved so you don’t have to re‑scan COMs.
  - Then when you press Dump/Flash for that lane, **all new info for that PCB** (log, MAC, status, etc.) will be filled for that same row.

So:

- **“Resetting lane = row becomes empty”** is true when you clear the serial (blank).  
- When you enter a **new serial**, the row is reset except for COM (by design); all new test info will belong to that serial once you run Dump/Flash.

If you instead want the row to truly be empty (including COM) every time the serial changes (even non‑blank), I can switch it so COM is also cleared on any serial change.

## Fix: Serial cleared in lanes 2, 3, 4

**Cause:** On blur (including when Enter is pressed), the script read `row.pcb_serial_no` from the model. For lanes 2–4, the model often wasn’t updated yet when blur fired, so `row.pcb_serial_no` was empty and the serial was treated as cleared.

**Change:** Use the value from the DOM input first, then fall back to the model:

```javascript
const dom_val = ($inp.val() || "").toString().trim();
const model_val = (row.pcb_serial_no || "").toString().trim();
const new_serial = dom_val || model_val;
```

This uses the value the user typed in the input, even if the model hasn’t synced yet.

### AI  ``

Here’s how it works **today** with **`left`** / **`right`** only.

### The scan only gives a **list of COM numbers**

There is **no** per-lane flag like “lane 2 empty.” So the connector **cannot** reliably produce:

- `112, nil, 114, 107` (hole in the **middle**)

unless something (driver/USB layout) actually returns **four slots** with a **placeholder** for the missing one—which **`com_scan_headless` does not** do today.

### What actually happens if physical **port 2 or 3** is empty

Windows still reports **one COM per connected device**, e.g. **three** numbers in some order, e.g. `['112','114','107']`.

| Mode   | Lanes 1–4 (3 ports)   |
|--------|-------------------------|
| **left**  | `112`, `114`, `107`, *(clear)* |
| **right** | *(clear)*, `112`, `114`, `107` |

So you always get:

- **left**: fill **from lane 1**, then **clear the tail**.
- **right**: **clear the head**, then pack **toward lane 4**.

Neither mode inserts **nil only in lane 2 or 3** while keeping the others aligned to physical slots 1, 3, 4—that would need a **fixed 4-position map** from hardware (or a scan that emits **four** entries including empty strings for missing slots).

### Practical takeaway

- **Middle empty** (only 2 or 3 unplugged): the ERP row may show a COM on a lane that **does not** match that physical socket, because the list is **packed** with no middle hole.
- To support **true** `112, nil, 114, 107` you’d need to extend **`com_scan_headless`** (and the connector) to output **exactly four** values aligned to your **fixed USB/hub order**, e.g. `["112", "", "114", "107"]`, then map **lane i ← list[i-1]** including empty strings.

If you want that next step, we can sketch or implement a **four-slot** JSON format from the scan and a **`COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "slot"`** (or similar) that assigns by index only and clears when the entry is empty.

### AI  ``

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### What went wrong
1. **Stale COM on lane 4**  
   Auto-COM only wrote when there was a **new non-empty** value. For lane 4 with only **3** scanned ports, `newv` was `""`, so the code did `continue` and **never cleared** the old `107`.

2. **106, 114, 107 on lanes 1–3**  
   With **left** packing, the three numbers always fill **from lane 1**. You wanted **lane 1 empty** and **106, 114, 107 on lanes 2–4** when physical port 1 has no device (same order as your `nil, 106, 114, 107` idea).

### What we implemented
1. **Clear COM when the scan assigns nothing**  
   If an idle lane’s target value is empty, we still **patch `com_port` to blank** when it used to have a value, so lane 4 (and any other unmapped lane) does not keep an old port.

2. **`COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE`**  
   - **`left`** (old behavior): `ports[0]` → lane 1, …; extra lanes cleared.  
   - **`right`**: if there are **fewer than 4** COM ports, **leave the low lanes empty** and **pack toward lane 4**  
     - e.g. 3 ports → lane 1 `""`, lanes 2–4 = `106`, `114`, `107`.

Default in the repo is **`"right"`**, which matches your “port 1 empty” case. If your rig always maps scan order to **lane 1 first**, set:

`COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE = "left"`

You’ll still get **trailing lanes cleared** when the count drops.

3. **Empty scan**  
   If the scan returns **no** ports, **idle** lanes get **COM cleared** (same logic: `ports_norm` empty → every lane gets `newv == ""`).

Startup now logs `COM_PORT_ASSIGN_MODE` so you can confirm it on the Lenono PC.

Copy the updated `PTS1 Station Connector.py` (or your `pts1_station_connector2_autocom.py` mirror) to the machine you run.

### 3) `request_action` – patch first, then validate serial/COM

Replace your entire `request_action` function with this version:

```javascript
async function request_action(frm, lane_no, action) {
  if (frm.is_new()) {
    return frappe.msgprint("Please click Save first, then press Dump/Flash.");
  }

  // commit currently typed cell into model
  await commit_active_grid_cell();

  // re-fetch row after blur commit
  let row = lane_row(frm, lane_no);
  if (!row) return frappe.msgprint(`Lane ${lane_no} row not found.`);

  // push lane values to DB first so server validation reads correct values
  try {
    await lane_patch_to_db(frm, lane_no);
  } catch (e) {
    console.error("[PTS1] lane_patch_to_db failed", e);
    return frappe.msgprint("Could not save lane fields. Try again.");
  }

  // re-check after patch (model is now stable)
  row = lane_row(frm, lane_no);
  if (!row) return frappe.msgprint(`Lane ${lane_no} row not found.`);

  const sn = (row.pcb_serial_no || "").toString().trim();
  const cp = (row.com_port || "").toString().trim();

  if (!sn || !cp) {
    return frappe.msgprint(`Lane ${lane_no}: PCB Serial No and COM Port are required.`);
  }

  if (isBusy(row)) {
    return frappe.msgprint(`Lane ${lane_no} is already ${row.lane_action_status}.`);
  }

  console.log("[PTS1] request_lane_action via pts1_api", { lane_no, action });

  return frappe
    .call({
      method: "pts1_api",
      args: {
        api_cmd: "request_lane_action",
        docname: frm.doc.name,
        lane_no: lane_no,
        action: action
      },
      freeze: true,
      freeze_message: `Queueing ${action} on Lane ${lane_no}...`
    })
    .then(() => {
      // instant UI update (no reload)
      const r = lane_row(frm, lane_no);
      if (r) {
        r.lane_action = action;
        r.lane_action_status = "Requested";
        r.lane_status = "Queued";
        r.lane_progress = 0;
        r.lane_action_message = "";
        r.error_message = "";
      }
      frm.refresh_field("lanes");
      render_lane_dashboard(frm);
      start_auto_refresh_if_needed(frm);
      frappe.show_alert({ message: `Lane ${lane_no} queued for ${action}`, indicator: "blue" });
    })
    .catch((e) => {
      console.error("[PTS1] request_lane_action failed", e);
      frappe.msgprint(`Failed to queue ${action} on Lane ${lane_no}. Check server script / connector logs.`);
    });
}
```

After these three edits:

- Blur is purely local and stable.
- Serial tracking map is correctly reset.
- Dump/Flash always patches latest lane values to DB before the server validates, even if you click directly from an active input.

Here’s what was aligned with **PCB Master / PCB Ledger** `pts1_status` options: **Pass**, **Fail**, **NA**, **Pending**.

### Mapping (Lane Result → `pts1_status`)

| Rule | `pts1_status` |
|------|----------------|
| Lane **not** `Completed` | **NA** |
| **Either** dump or flash is **Fail** | **Fail** |
| **Either** is **Pending** (and no Fail) | **Pending** |
| **Either** is **NA** (and no Fail/Pending) | **NA** |
| **Both** **Pass** | **Pass** |
| Anything else (empty / unknown / mixed) | **NA** |

**Note:** Lane not completed now sets **`NA`** (not **Fail**). If you prefer **Fail** when the lane is not `Completed`, say so and we can switch that branch only.

### Simple fix (recommended)

The failure is ONLY because of the ✅ emoji. Do this:

1. **Find `update_file` function** in your dump script (the one that prints or writes MAC info / “update passed” into a file).
2. Inside `update_file`, look for any string that contains **✅** (or other emoji) that is being **written to a file** (e.g. `f.write("✅ ...")` or similar).
3. **Replace the emoji with plain text**, for example:
   - Change `"✅ MAC updated"` → `"MAC updated OK"` or `"[PASS] MAC updated"`.
4. Save the file and run the dump again.

That’s it: once the file write no longer uses the emoji, `update_file` will stop throwing the `charmap` error, and your dump will end as **PASSED** instead of **FAILED**.
